sections.label: Changi Airport Terminal 5 plans
sections.summary: Terminal 5 will break ground, raising Changi Airport's capacity by 50% and keeping Singapore a gateway for travel and trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the beginning of this term of Government, COVID-19 put plans for Changi Airport Terminal 5 on hold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This year, the Finance Minister announced that Terminal 5 will break ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With its completion, Changi Airport's capacity will increase by 50%, ensuring that Singapore will remain a critical gateway for global travel and trade.

sections.label: 2024 economic statistics
sections.summary: The Finance Minister gave 2024 figures: 4.4% growth, easing inflation, wages outpacing inflation, and lowest income inequality since 2000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister dished out the broad statistics for 2024 in his speech: 4.4% growth; inflation continuing to ease; wage increases outpacing inflation; median income of resident workers rising 3.4% above inflation; and income inequality being at its lowest since 2000.

sections.label: Total fertility rate below one
sections.summary: For the first time in Singapore's history, the total fertility rate fell below one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the first time in our history, our total fertility rate (TFR) fell below one.

sections.label: F&B business closures in 2024
sections.summary: Over 3,000 F&B businesses closed in 2024, more than eight daily, the highest number since 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More than 3,000 food and beverage (F&B) businesses closed their doors for good in 2024, citing dwindling business and higher operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is more than eight F&B businesses shutting every single day, the highest number since 2015.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus projections
sections.summary: A $6.8 billion surplus is projected for FY2025, while 2024's surplus was revised from $778 million to $6.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A fiscal surplus of $6.8 billion is projected for the financial year (FY) 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for 2024, even after the latest CDC and SG60 Voucher programme, 2024's fiscal surplus, originally estimated at a healthy $778 million, has been revised massively upwards to $6.4 billion.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus for this term
sections.summary: The overall fiscal surplus for 2021 to 2025 is set to reach around $14.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The overall fiscal surplus for the years 2021 to 2025, or this term of Government, is set to hit around $14.3 billion.

sections.label: BEPS 2.0 corporate tax revenue
sections.summary: The Government reviewed its BEPS 2.0 position and anticipates higher corporate income tax revenue from FY2027 if Singapore stays attractive to MNEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has also reviewed its position on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS 2.0), and is anticipating even higher corporate income tax revenue from FY2027, provided Singapore remains attractive to MNEs.

sections.label: Defence Minister Munich Security Conference comments
sections.summary: The Defence Minister's Munich comments on the US behaving like a landlord portend a world possibly changing for the worse and a security architecture possibly needing reconfiguration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The comments of the Defence Minister at the Munich Security Conference less than a fortnight ago – of the US now behaving like a landlord seeking rent and no longer being the force of moral legitimacy that it used to be – portend a world that may not be changing for the better and a security architecture that may have to be reconfigured.

sections.label: US Defence Secretary on China deterrence
sections.summary: The US Defence Secretary said the US prioritises deterring war with China in the Pacific, reinforcing the importance of the SAF, Home Team and National Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Only two days prior to the Minister's speech, the new US Defence Secretary at the Ukraine Defence Contact Group said, in the context of pivoting away from Europe, and I quote: "we also face a peer competitor in the Communist Chinese with the capability and intent to threaten our homeland and core national interests in the Indo-Pacific.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The US is prioritising deterring war with China in the Pacific, recognising the reality of scarcity and making the resourcing trade-offs to ensure deterrence does not fail".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The wider strategic atmospherics lead me to reiterate that our national unity, a subject I mentioned briefly in my speech, in these unpredictable times is actually vital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This outlook reinforces the importance of the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), the Home Team and the importance of National Service (NS).

sections.label: Budget benefits and economic investments
sections.summary: A six-person middle-income three-generation family in a 5-room HDB flat can receive about $10,000 in benefits, while the Budget funds the National Productivity Fund, R&D, Enterprise Compute Initiative and Changi Airport Development Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For example, a six-person, middle-income, three-generation family living in a 5-room HDB flat can receive total benefits of about $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Besides tackling the immediate concerns, the Budget also allocates substantial resources to push our economic growth frontier, investing in technology, enterprises and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: There is the $3 billion top-up for National Productivity Fund to help us anchor high-quality investments in Singapore; the $1 billion investment is to keep our R&D infrastructure at cutting edge; and up to $150 million is allocated to the new Enterprise Compute Initiative to help enterprises develop bespoke AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To boost our air hub status, the Changi Airport Development Fund will be topped up by another $5 billion.

sections.label: NTUC additional funding
sections.summary: NTUC will get an additional $200 million to set up more company training committees and push for more skills advancement at company level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) will also get an additional $200 million funding to set up more company training committees and to push for more skills advancement at the company level.

sections.label: Diversifying tax base and rates
sections.summary: The report said the Government has to diversify its tax base and increase tax rates to improve sustainability and maintain a balanced budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For example, it also mentioned in the report that to sustain Singapore's increasing expenditures and the pressure to spend even more, the Government has to "diversify its tax base and increase tax rates to improve sustainability and to maintain a balanced budget".

sections.label: Overall surpluses and GST rates
sections.summary: It notes overall surpluses of $6.4 billion for FY2024 and $6.8 billion for FY2025, which raise questions about whether GST rates were raised prematurely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And it reflects a refreshing relationship between the new Prime Minister's Government and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is about the overall surpluses for FY2024 and FY2025, of $6.4 billion and $6.8 billion respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Such large surpluses would, understandably, bring into question whether we have prematurely raised the GST rates.

sections.label: Corporate income tax collections
sections.summary: It states that corporate income tax collections rose to $30.88 billion, $2.5 billion above the earlier estimate, with $32.67 billion estimated for the next FY.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The main contributor to the large overall surpluses is the significant increase in the corporate income tax collections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The latest revised figures for corporate income tax, in this year's Budget paper, now stands at $30.88 billion, an increase of $2.5 billion from the earlier estimate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The estimate for corporate income tax for the next FY is a higher figure of $32.67 billion.

sections.label: Nationally Significant Infrastructure capitalisation figures
sections.summary: Annex H-1 reports capitalisation of Nationally Significant Infrastructure estimated at $4.17 billion for FY2024 and $4.63 billion for FY2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In Annex H-1, it also reported high figures for the capitalisation of Nationally Significant Infrastructure, estimated to be $4.17 billion for FY2024 and $4.63 billion in FY2025.

sections.label: Public transport fare subsidy
sections.summary: It recalls a request to consider once-off fare assistance and notes the Government provided a $250 million additional subsidy over the $2 billion yearly subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: At last year's Budget debate, I asked the Government to keep watch of the public transport fare and to consider a once-off assistance to moderate the fare increase if the Budget position permits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I am glad and thankful that the Government did provide a once-off additional subsidy of $250 million, over and above the $2 billion a year subsidy, to moderate the fare increase.

sections.label: PSP housing schemes criticised
sections.summary: It says the PSP's Affordable Housing and Millennial Apartments Schemes risk destabilising the housing market and create a two-tier market without solving core issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: For example, the Progress Singapore Party's (PSP's) Affordable Housing Scheme and Millennial Apartments Scheme may seem appealing at the surface, but they risk destabilising the housing market without solving the core issues at hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: By removing land costs from the upfront price of new flats, the Affordable Homes Scheme creates a two-tier housing market where older resale flats must compete with significantly cheaper new ones.

sections.label: Raising BTO income ceiling
sections.summary: It says some couples earn above the BTO eligibility threshold but cannot afford private condominiums, so raising the income ceiling would keep public housing accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Some young and capable Singaporean couples today find themselves earning just above the eligibility threshold for Build-To-Order (BTO) flats but not enough to comfortably afford a private condominium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: By increasing the income ceiling, we can ensure that young professionals, some of whom do not have deep financial support from their families, still have access to public housing options.

sections.label: Supporting private estate residents
sections.summary: MND support for initiatives helps private estate residents feel connected, including the Estate Upgrading Programme for Silver Estates and EASE 2.0 extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: By supporting such initiatives, MND can help private estate residents feel more connected to the broader community, strengthening the social fabric of our neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I am particularly delighted about the introduction of the Estate Upgrading Programme for Silver Estates as well as the extension of the Enhancement for Active Seniors 2.0 programme to private estates which benefit seniors in Kebun Baru.

sections.label: Active Ageing Centres and senior care
sections.summary: Suggests Active Ageing Centres work with domestic helpers with consent, and regulating senior and home care services for listing, pricing and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One idea is to develop a framework where Active Ageing Centres can work with domestic helpers, with the full consent of seniors and their families, so that the small team of Active Ageing Centre staff can tap into a larger pool of caregivers to organise activities, providing companionship, and extending support beyond the physical Active Ageing Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Additionally, we should also look at regulating senior care and home care services, ensuring that all service providers are digitally listed, transparent in pricing, and accountable for the quality of care provided.

sections.label: SCDF digital access for seniors
sections.summary: Proposes empowering SCDF emergency services with digital access to homes of frail seniors when a fall detection alert is triggered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we should empower SCDF emergency services with digital access to homes of frail seniors, should a fall detection alert be triggered.

sections.label: National AI system for Singapore
sections.summary: States Singapore must develop a national AI system that is sovereign, human-centric and cost-effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To achieve this, Singapore must develop a national AI system, one that is sovereign, human-centric and cost-effective.

sections.label: Centre of Excellence for AI Alignment
sections.summary: Proposes a Centre of Excellence for AI Alignment to develop frameworks, and using commercial AI data centres to keep costs manageable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: A key component of this initiative could be the establishment of a Centre of Excellence for AI Alignment, which will develop AI frameworks that ensure that AI models adhere to our needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To keep costs manageable, we can leverage commercial AI data centres for training and finetuning of AI models, rather than investing heavily on on-premise compute infrastructure.

sections.label: Ageing care and sovereign AI
sections.summary: Calls for rethinking care models so seniors live independently with dignity, and developing a sovereign AI system serving Singapore's interests and values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In ageing, we must move beyond infrastructure and rethink care models that empower seniors to live independently with dignity, even in private estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And in AI, we must act decisively to develop a sovereign AI system that serves Singapore's interests while ensuring alignment with our values, security needs and our ability to shape the world.

sections.label: SG60 and CDC Vouchers
sections.summary: The passage states that SG60 Vouchers and additional CDC Vouchers are not enough to help Singaporeans long-term or solve structural economic issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While many Singaporeans will welcome the $600 or $800 SG60 Vouchers and additional $800 CDC Vouchers, they are not enough to help Singaporeans in the long-term or solve Singapore's structural economic issues.

sections.label: PSP Affordable Homes Scheme
sections.summary: PSP's proposed Affordable Homes Scheme would price new HDB flats to recover only construction cost, not land cost, at first purchase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP's proposed Affordable Homes Scheme will price new HDB flats to recover only the construction cost but not the land cost at first purchase.

sections.label: Hawker rental system proposal
sections.summary: The passage states the policy has consequences on food prices, so PSP advocates a fixed rental of $500 monthly or 3% of gross turnover.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But this policy has consequences on food prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That is why PSP has advocated for a fixed rental system of $500 per month or 3% of the hawker's gross turnover per month.

sections.label: PSP GST position
sections.summary: PSP has long proposed to either maintain GST at 7% or reduce GST from 9% to 7%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP has long proposed to either maintain GST at 7% or to reduce GST from 9% to 7%.

sections.label: Government surpluses and GST
sections.summary: The passage states FY2024/2025 and next FY surpluses underline there was no necessity to raise GST from 7% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government's $6.4 billion surplus for FY2024/2025 and the expected $6.8 billion surplus for the next FY further underlines that there was no necessity to raise GST from 7% to 9% Let us also not forget that larger surpluses that go into the reserves mean bigger cost burdens on taxpayers when the Government collects more than is needed to spend on public programmes.

sections.label: PSP public holidays proposal
sections.summary: PSP proposes to increase public holidays from 11 to 14, with one additional holiday for each of the three major races.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP proposes to increase the number of public holidays from 11 to 14, with one additional holiday for each of the three major races in Singapore.

sections.label: Right to disconnect legislation
sections.summary: It proposes a right to disconnect for employees on paid leave, later extended to hours outside normal working hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Workers in Singapore already work very long hours compared to others around the world, but this may not even include time spent at home responding to work-related texts or emails, which prevent workers from spending quality time with their families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We can first introduce the "right to disconnect" legislation for employees who are on paid leave and eventually extend to the "right to disconnect" between 7.00 pm and 7.00 am or outside the normal working hours of the employee.

sections.label: Affordable Homes Scheme proposal
sections.summary: PSP proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme, pricing new HDB flats at construction cost only, excluding land cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For instance, regarding public housing, PSP has proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme, where new HDB flats will be priced at construction cost only, excluding land cost.

sections.label: PSP support for Budget
sections.summary: PSP will support the Budget because short-term assistance is necessary for Singaporeans coping with rising living costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding our reservations, PSP will support the Budget because short-term assistance is necessary for Singaporeans to cope with the rising cost of living, until structural changes are implemented.

sections.label: Caregiving tax reliefs and grant
sections.summary: It notes tax reliefs for supporting parents at home and supports the enhanced Home Caregiving Grant of up to $600 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Currently, we have tax reliefs in place for those who support their parents at home and I am fully supportive of the enhanced Home Caregiving Grant which provides direct cash support of up to $600 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The maximum household income per capita has also been raised to $4,800.

sections.label: Property tax and estate upgrading
sections.summary: It hopes for frequent property tax reviews and notes 32 private estates getting new or improved facilities under the Estate Upgrading Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that there will be continued and frequent reviews of our property tax regime to ensure that it remains equitable and sustainable, especially for groups that do not necessarily have the cash resources to afford taxes in the long run.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There are 32 private estates in Singapore who will have new or improved facilities, such as new recreational spaces, wheelchair-accessible ramps and estate markers in the next five years under the Estate Upgrading Programme.

sections.label: Support for sandwiched families
sections.summary: It asks for accelerated Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme or support for flats, and targeted help for sandwiched families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Could the Government consider offering the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme on an accelerated timeline for these flats, or additional support to help ensure that the infrastructure of these flats remain liveable for our residents?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government needs to continue looking after the needs of our sandwiched group, given that their very specific financial circumstances are addressed with targeted, meaningful solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These proposed initiatives are designed to provide both immediate and long-term relief, ensuring that no family is left behind as the cost of living continues to rise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: By introducing comprehensive caregiver relief, enhancing transportation subsidies and improving their living environment, we can create a Singapore where our sandwiched families are empowered to thrive, rather than being left behind due to the pressures of daily life.

sections.label: Income inequality and economic growth
sections.summary: Income inequality is at its lowest since 2000 and economic growth was 4.4% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Income inequality is at its lowest since 2000 and we achieved better-than-expected economic growth of 4.4% last year.

sections.label: EDB 2024 investment commitments statistics
sections.summary: EDB 2024 statistics show falls in projected value-added, jobs and business expenditure, with some MNCs scaling down or shutting operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to the Economic Development Board's Year-in-Review 2024 statistics on commitments to invest into Singapore, we are seeing falls across the projected contribution of value-added per annum, the number of jobs expected to be created and total business expenditure per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While Amazon Web Services and pharma giant AstraZeneca have announced major investment commitments into Singapore, other MNCs, like Dyson, Samsung Electronics, Shein and Electrolux, have either scaled down or shut down their Singapore operations.

sections.label: BEPS 2.0 and corporate tax rebate
sections.summary: The 50% corporate income tax rebate is a positive surprise given recent BEPS 2.0 moves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In view of our recent moves to implement BEPS 2.0, the 50% corporate income tax rebate announced by the Prime Minister is a positive surprise.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up usage
sections.summary: Minister Chan Chun Sing said about 26% of eligible Singaporeans used the $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up given in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In response to a PQ last month, Minister Chan Chun Sing shared that only about 26% of eligible Singaporeans have used their one-off SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500, even though the top-up was given in 2020 and expires by the end of this year.

sections.label: Resident households with children and parents
sections.summary: Department of Statistics 2024 data show at least 51.7% of resident households comprise children staying with their parents or parent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Based on the Department of Statistics' 2024 data, at least 51.7% of resident households comprise children staying together with their parents or parent.

sections.label: Budget 2025 family support
sections.summary: Budget 2025 provides support for families and more for vulnerable families, with hope the Large Families Scheme raises the Total Fertility Rate from 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, Budget 2025 provides support for families and even more for vulnerable families, and I am very thankful for that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I share the National Population and Talent Division (NPTD) and Minister Indranee’s hope that the Large Families Scheme will encourage more Singaporeans to have three or more children and bring our Total Fertility Rate up from 0.97.

sections.label: Family-friendly work and parental leave
sections.summary: The passage calls for addressing issues discouraging people from having children and asks whether parental and family care leave can be increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We should, therefore, work continuously to address the various issues that are currently discouraging our people from having children or from having more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But besides financial support, perhaps one area that the Government can facilitate more is in creating a family-friendly environment at work and, like I mentioned earlier, the feedback from the Budget dialogue last year, could we, perhaps, look at increasing parental leave and family care leave for working, adult caregivers?

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements complaints
sections.summary: The passage asks how many complaints MOM has received about employers not complying with the Tripartite Guidelines on FWA Requests launched in April 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Another area which will alleviate the burden on working caregivers is flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, since the Tripartite Guidelines on FWA Requests were launched in April 2024, how many complaints has the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) received regarding employers who are not complying with the guidelines?

sections.label: CPF LIFE Escalating Plan enhancement
sections.summary: The passage asks how the CPF LIFE Escalating Plan, which increases payouts by 2% annually, can be enhanced given inflation and market interest rates above 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Given the long-term inflation outlook and the fact that market interest rates continue to be above 2%, how can we enhance the CPF LIFE Escalating Plan, which increases payouts by 2% annually?

sections.label: ComCare reviews and Uplifting Employment Credit
sections.summary: The passage asks how often financial assistance amounts are reviewed, how the upcoming increase is determined, and how much the Uplifting Employment Credit has been tapped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Anyone who has been involved in constituency or community work would know the important role that ComCare plays in taking care of those in need around us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, may I ask how often are the financial assistance amounts reviewed and how is the quantum of the upcoming increase determined?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How much has the Uplifting Employment Credit been tapped on since it was introduced in Budget 2023?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support for overseas Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage proposes extending the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme to overseas Singaporeans, noting a residency requirement of prior employment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One avenue where we can include them is to extend the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme to Singaporeans working overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A resident has recently informed me that Workforce Singapore had told him that overseas Singaporeans will not be eligible for monetary help under the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme because one of the requirements is that you had to be previously employed in Singapore for at least six of the past 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If we would like more younger Singaporeans to dare to venture abroad to build Singapore's competitiveness in the longer term, we should extend the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support to cover the more than 200,000 overseas Singaporeans.

sections.label: Inflation and cost of living concerns
sections.summary: The passage notes that Members and others have raised inflation and cost of living, including concerns about GST and its impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Earlier, Members have highlighted and many of those outside this Chamber have also raised the point about inflation and the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And I think some Members here today have highlighted that as well about inflation being turbocharged due to GST and the question is whether that has actually raised concerns about whether that will continue to have an impact on the cost of living.

sections.label: Budget 2025 consistency and GST inflation
sections.summary: A PQ reply said the GST increase adds slightly under one percentage point to core inflation, and Budget 2025 stays consistent with past Budgets and Forward Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: In fact, in a PQ on 6 February 2024 which Member Mr Liang Eng Hwa had raised, the response highlighted that GST rate increase is estimated to contribute only slightly less than one percentage point to core inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: There are other factors, such as high electricity and gas tariffs which are due to increase in oil prices, as well as production costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Global supply chains are shifting as countries seek to protect their supply chain resilience as well as their domestic economy and priorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: But despite all that uncertainty, Budget 2025 demonstrates consistency – consistency with past Budgets to continue the good work we have done to bring an unexpected level of growth amid our lowest level of income inequality since the turn of the century; consistency with our ideals as identified in the Forward Singapore exercise to help involuntarily-unemployed jobseekers bounce back stronger, supporting families and seniors, empowering and uplifting those in need; and consistency in our Government philosophy that the long-term interests of Singaporeans must remain the key priority regardless of how the upcoming General Election will turn out.

sections.label: Nurturing Singaporeans as global leaders
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to consider a more programmatic national and international approach to give Singaporeans exposure and training to become global leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But at the same time, I hope that the Government will not neglect the efforts to nurture and develop Singaporeans with the potential to lead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would like the Government to consider introducing a more programmatic approach on a national and international level to provide Singaporeans with the exposure and training that they need to step up to be global leaders.

sections.label: SkillsFuture courses and employment outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker notes thousands of SkillsFuture and micro-credential courses and many funding schemes, and asks how strongly they drive employment outcomes for mid-career and senior Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, there are thousands of SkillsFuture and micro-credential courses offered by training providers and a plethora of funding schemes that Singaporeans can leverage on in their skill acquisition journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But while this is good, my question is: how strongly are the SkillsFuture and micro-credential courses driving employment outcomes, especially for mid-career and senior Singaporeans?

sections.label: Auditing courses and supporting unemployed
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether SSG audits courses for employment outcomes, would tighten and deregister weak courses, and whether programmes exist to help long-term unemployed individuals return to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the same scheme, I would like to know whether SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) has conducted audits on the courses offered to find out their correlation with tangible employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would SSG thus consider tightening the number and the genres of courses offered and deregister courses that do not lead to strong employment outcomes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And lastly, apart from what Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) is currently doing, are there specific programmes to support long-term unemployed individuals or those who have chosen to take a break from the full-time employment to get back to work?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is a wonderful accomplishment for us to come this far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But while we bask in a general mood of celebrations, let us not forget that there are dark clouds gathering on our horizon and take heed that SG60 did not happen because it is meant to happen, but rather, it happened because we, collectively, as a country made it happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: SG60 belongs to all Singaporeans, past and present, and to everyone who has, in their own way, made this happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that Singapore will continue to defy the odds, thrive in this age of uncertainty and be an exemplar of how a country can stand united, with every member of the society being given the support and opportunity to succeed, regardless of our station in life.

sections.label: Unemployment and median household income
sections.summary: The passage states that unemployment has fallen to less than 3% and median household income has risen to $11,297.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Today, thanks to decades of hard work and sound policies, unemployment has fallen to less than 3% and our median household income has risen to $11,297.

sections.label: Enabling Master Plan and Employment Credit
sections.summary: The passage states MSF developed the Enabling Master Plan 2030, implemented by Mr Eric Chua, and that Prime Minister Lawrence Wong agreed to extend the Enabling Employment Credit to end-2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In recent years, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) has developed the Enabling Master Plan 2030, effectively implemented by its Senior Parliamentary Secretary Mr Eric Chua.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am also grateful that Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has agreed to extend the Enabling Employment Credit to the end of 2028, ensuring employers continue to receive wage offsets for hiring PSN.

sections.label: Caregiver grant proposal
sections.summary: The speaker urges MSF to consider a quarterly $200 grant for caregivers, similar to the Silver Support Scheme, through LifeSG credits or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: There are countless caregivers across Singapore who are equally — who are also quietly bearing the weight of their responsibilities with little recognition or support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: That is why I urge MSF to consider providing caregivers with a quarterly grant of $200, similar to the Silver Support Scheme, through LifeSG credits or otherwise.

sections.label: Segmented unit households hardships
sections.summary: Many households in the 2,000 segmented units across 140 blocks share similar hardships and challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Many households staying in the 2,000 segmented units across 140 blocks in Singapore share similar hardships and challenges.

sections.label: Segmented unit repurposing and assistance
sections.summary: The speaker proposes leasing segmented units to workers via agencies like JTC, giving cash assistance for relocation, and waiving the resale levy for BTO purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thirdly, repurpose these segmented units by leasing them to workers through agencies like JTC, rather than reselling them and repeating the cycle again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Fourthly, provide cash assistance to owners of segmented units, with higher assistance for families with members who have physical disabilities, to help them relocate to flats with direct lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last but not least, waive the resale levy, if applicable, when owners sell their segmented units to purchase a BTO flat with lift access to reduce their financial burden.

sections.label: Caregiver grant for blue CHAS holders
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MSF consider a quarterly $200 grant for caregivers holding a blue CHAS card, similar to the Silver Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: To lighten their burden, I suggest MSF consider providing a quarterly grant of $200 to caregivers who hold a blue CHAS card, similar to the Silver Support Scheme.

sections.label: NDC emissions downward trajectory
sections.summary: The NDC is a commitment to the international process, and the Government has committed to a downward emissions trajectory after the 2028 plan peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The NDC is a concrete commitment we have made to the international process and I am glad that for the first time the Government has committed to a downward trajectory in the country's emissions after the plan peak in 2028.

sections.label: Heavy vehicle electrification schemes
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Heavy Vehicle Zero Emission Scheme and Electric Heavy Vehicle Charger Grant for heavy vehicle purchase and charging infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I have also previously spoken on my concern for the slower electrification of our logistics vehicles, including lorries and other heavy vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I welcome the Prime Minister's announcement of a new Heavy Vehicle Zero Emission Scheme and an Electric Heavy Vehicle Charger Grant, providing incentives for the purchase of heavy vehicles and co-funding of charging infrastructure.

sections.label: Changi Airport Development Fund top-up
sections.summary: The Government will provide $5 billion more to the Changi Airport Development Fund, some going to Terminal 5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Government will provide $5 billion more to the Changi Airport Development Fund, some of which would go to Terminal 5, which the Prime Minister has said that when completed, will increase our airport capacity by 50%.

sections.label: Support for adults with disabilities
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Government study of post-18 pathways for persons with disabilities and notes existing workplace funding and the extended Enabling Employment Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I spoke on doing more for the care and education of adults with special needs, including post-SPED school education and training as well as doing more for their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I am therefore happy to hear that the Government is looking into the post-18 pathways for persons with disabilities, to see how more support can be given to those transiting to work, building up work readiness at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Reasonable accommodations are essential for a person with disability in entering the workforce and attaining and maintaining employment, and this would be consistent with the requirements the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I note that there are already state funding and subsidies for improvements to workplace, job redesign, assistive technology to aid persons with disabilities in their workplace and there is also the Enabling Employment Credit, which has just been extended to end-2028 under this Budget, and these are all beneficial for persons with disabilities in the workplace.

sections.label: Subsidies for long-term care services
sections.summary: The speaker supports raising maximum subsidies to 95% for non-residential and 80% for residential long-term care, with qualifying income raised to $1,500 per capita.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, I hope MOH and other stakeholders can give some thought as to how centres can be given more resources so that they can take care of more residents assigned to their cluster and residents can use their centres for activities more optimally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We are heartened to note that the Budget has stepped up quite significantly to this end and we support the raising of the maximum subsidy level to 95% for the non-residential long term care services for per capita household incomes below $1,500, to allow more people to age in place with financial support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We also welcome the maximum subsidy level of 80% for residential long-term care, which we had proposed in our manifesto.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We are heartened that the qualifying income for their maximum level of subsidy has been raised to $1,500 per capita.

sections.label: Removing annual value criteria
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will remove the annual value criteria and give the same subsidies to all households with no income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For all these reasons, I hope the Government will reconsider and to remove the annual value criteria and provide the same subsidies to all household that have no income.

sections.label: National Adult Oral Health Survey 2019
sections.summary: The National Adult Oral Health Survey of 2019 found three-quarters of those aged 21 to 64 in Singapore have periodontal disease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Is it surprising that the National Adult Oral Health Survey of 2019 revealed that three-quarters of those aged between 21 and 64 in Singapore suffer from periodontal disease?

sections.label: Subsidies for CHAS green card holders
sections.summary: The subsidy framework should be expanded to CHAS green card holders so subsidised care is available at private dental clinics under the Primary Care Partnership scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: First, the subsidy framework should be expanded to holders of the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) green card, so that subsidised care may be available for all at private dental clinics under the Primary Care Partnership scheme.

sections.label: Dental care omission from Healthier SG
sections.summary: Prof Chris Peck said in a Straits Times Forum letter that dental care's omission from Healthier SG needs rectification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In his Straits Times Forum letter on 22 November 2024, the dean of the National University of Singapore dental faculty, Prof Chris Peck said that the omission of dental care from Healthier SG "needs rectification".

sections.label: SG60 vouchers for independence celebration
sections.summary: SG60 vouchers are to be given out in celebration of Singapore's 60 years of Independence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Of special mention is the SG60 vouchers that are to be given up in celebration of our 60 years of Independence.

sections.label: Singapore economy and income inequality
sections.summary: An MTI report says the economy grew 4.4%, median incomes rose 3.4% above inflation, and income inequality hit its lowest since 2000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As highlighted in the latest MTI report, Singapore's economy grew by 4.4% last year, with median incomes rising 3.4% above inflation and income inequality reaching its lowest since the year 2000.

sections.label: Ageing population and cost challenges
sections.summary: An ageing population, a total fertility rate below one at 0.97, and high cost of living form potent challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: An ageing population, low total fertility rate – now, very low, at below one, at 0.97 – high cost of living, these are potent combinations of challenges that we face.

sections.label: Government support for seniors and healthcare
sections.summary: The Government has a robust system supporting seniors and the population for healthcare, subsidies, the three Ms, longer-term care and caregiver home grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This is our future, so we must avoid this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I must say that our Government has put in place a robust system to support our seniors and the entire population for healthcare, subsidies, the three Ms and also, with this budget, we have greater support in terms of the longer-term care, as well as the caregiver home grant support.

sections.label: Technology, R&D and energy investments
sections.summary: Singapore leads in semiconductors and life sciences, and the Budget tops up the Future Energy Fund by $5 billion for energy security and carbon neutrality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, in technology and innovation leadership, Singapore is a global leader in semiconductor manufacturing and life sciences, producing over 10% the world's chips and 80% of DNA chips.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: A continued investment in R&D will anchor our relevance in global supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And, of course, in sustainable energy and climate resilience, something that has been termed as an existential one for us, the Budget's $5 billion top-up to the Future Energy Fund and investments in hydrogen, nuclear and renewable energy sources are forward-thinking steps toward energy security and carbon neutrality.

sections.label: Replenishing Reserves from surplus
sections.summary: The speaker repeats a call for the Government to return to the Reserves what was taken out during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Given that we had a relatively good fiscal year with surplus, I would like to reiterate my call on the Government to put back into the Reserves what we had taken out during the pandemic.

sections.label: SG60 vouchers cash distribution
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOF to reconsider giving part of the SG60 vouchers in cash so individuals can save, donate or use it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Specific to SG60 vouchers, which is quite unlike the GST or CDC Vouchers that are purposed to address everyday costs and also, in a large part, to help drive business to our micro-SMEs within the heartlands and beyond, it is a special commemorative benefit for Singaporeans age above 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But given that there are many vouchers already, would MOF reconsider distributing part of it in cash so that individuals can choose to save it, donate it or use it for other legitimate purposes?

sections.label: Gradual replenishment of Reserves
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to gradually return pandemic-drawn Reserves from surpluses in future years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Considering this year's fiscal surplus, I would like to again urge the Government to gradually replenish the Reserves used during the pandemic to assist Singaporeans and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I hope that at least some portion of the surplus can be returned to the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Even if not all at once, I hope it can be gradually returned in future years when there are surpluses.

sections.label: SG60 vouchers cash suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government reconsider distributing part of the SG60 vouchers in cash to give people options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The SG60 vouchers are a sincere gesture to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: However, I suggest the Government reconsider distributing part of the vouchers in cash, giving people options to save, donate or spend it.

sections.label: Support for Budget measures
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with proposals for businesses, upskilling and future preparation, and is grateful for surplus sharing including MediSave top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I agree with the proposals to help businesses plan for growth, the push to help our citizens upskill themselves and the plans to prepare Singapore for the future which is always changing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And I am grateful that, with a Budget surplus, the Government has decided to share more with its citizens, for example, by providing $3 billion in MediSave top-ups.

sections.label: Vouchers for all Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker is pleased the Finance Minister gave Climate Vouchers to all households and SG60 benefits to all Singaporeans regardless of housing type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I also recall my Budget speech a few years ago, where I had urged the Government to consider ways in which we can allow our retirees and middle-income Singaporeans to share or enjoy the growth of the country and to move together as a nation, regardless of where they stay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, for this year's Budget, I am really pleased that the Finance Minister has heard our pleas and given Climate Vouchers to all households, including those in private properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am also glad that the SG60 vouchers, SG60, ActiveSG credit top-ups and SG60 Culture Pass will be given to all Singaporeans, regardless of housing type.

sections.label: Foreign worker ratio and rental costs
sections.summary: The speaker says reviewing the foreign worker ratio will keep business labour costs down and urges adjusting JTC, HDB and hawker stall rentals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, reviewing the foreign worker ratio will enable businesses to keep their labour costs down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I also urge the Government to adjust rental costs for businesses on JTC- and HDB-owned industrial and commercial properties and also to consider reducing rental costs for hawker stalls.

sections.label: Scheme for couples having children
sections.summary: The speaker says the scheme eases couples' concerns through better financial support but questions whether it encourages more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Indeed, it will ease some of the concerns of the couples because of better financial support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, if this scheme is intended to encourage couples to have more children, I think the Government must go back to the drawing board to ask why are many couples not even having children.

sections.label: Work stress and planning children
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether work stress makes it difficult for couples to plan for children and says Singaporeans lead too stressful a life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Or is it due to work stress that makes it difficult for couples to plan for children?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I personally think that Singaporeans lead too stressful a life.

sections.label: Long working hours in Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker notes Parliament staff work long hours during late debates and urges the Government to review the culture of long, stressful hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Even in Parliament, Sir, our Clerks and other staff work such long hours because MPs debate long hours, spend time debating Bills until late in the evening and sometimes until late at night.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to please review this culture of working long and stressful hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Will a better lifestyle allow us to consider a bigger family?

sections.label: Budget surpluses for FY2024 and FY2025
sections.summary: The Finance Minister reported a $6.4 billion surplus for FY2024 and a projected $6.8 billion surplus for FY2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Despite these comprehensive measures, the Finance Minister reported a surplus of $6.4 billion for FY2024, and a projected $6.8 billion surplus for FY2025.

sections.label: Healthcare and defence spending growth
sections.summary: In FY2025, healthcare spending will grow by over 16% to about $21 billion and defence spending will rise by over 12%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In FY2025, this year, healthcare spending alone will grow by over 16% to about $21 billion, while defence spending will rise by over 12%.

sections.label: Equity requirement for single-family offices
sections.summary: The Equity Market Development Programme requires new single-family office applicants eligible for Permanent Residency to allocate at least $50 million to Singapore-listed equities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: An example is the new requirement under the Equity Market Development Programme, which mandates that all new single-family office applicants under the Global Investor Programme category eligible for Permanent Residency, allocate at least $50 million of their assets under management to equities listed on approved Singapore exchanges.

sections.label: Engaging established family offices
sections.summary: Only 200 individuals received Permanent Resident status through the Global Investor Programme from 2020 to 2022, so the 2,000 family offices in Singapore should be engaged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Furthermore, I note from an answer to a PQ that only 200 individuals were granted Permanent Resident status through the Global Investor Programme from 2020 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, to fully tap the family office capital for a more diversified investor base, we should consider engaging the 2,000 family offices already established in Singapore.

sections.label: Graduate employment outcomes softening
sections.summary: The latest Joint Autonomous University Graduate Employment Survey shows fresh graduates' employment outcomes are already softening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Indeed, based on the latest Joint Autonomous University Graduate Employment Survey, we are already seeing fresh graduates' employment outcomes softening.

sections.label: Budget 2025 sustainability commitment
sections.summary: Budget 2025 includes a $5 billion top-up to the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund and extends climate vouchers to private properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Budget 2025 reflects Singapore's firm commitment to sustainability with a $5 billion top-up to the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund and other initiatives, such as the extension of climate vouchers to private properties.

sections.label: High-value green industries
sections.summary: Renewable energy, green finance, sustainable infrastructure and carbon services are high-value industries where Singapore can play a leadership role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Renewable energy, green finance, sustainable infrastructure and carbon services are all high-value industries where Singapore can play a leadership role.

sections.label: 2024 GDP growth and benefits
sections.summary: Singapore's 2024 GDP growth of 4.4%, up from 1.8% in 2023, reflects an approach ensuring economic growth benefits all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It reflects our nation's approach to ensuring economic growth, translating into tangible benefits for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is a result of our strong economic performance in 2024, with Singapore registering GDP growth of 4.4%, a notable acceleration from the 1.8% growth we saw in 2023.

sections.label: M&A scheme extension
sections.summary: The Government's mergers and acquisitions scheme is extended until December 2030, showing commitment to supporting business growth through M&A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses appreciate the Government's extension of the mergers and acquisitions (M&As) scheme until December 2030, demonstrating our continued commitment to supporting business growth through M&A.

sections.label: Enterprise Financing Scheme enhancement
sections.summary: The Enterprise Financing Scheme has been enhanced to give SMEs better access to funding and working capital for internationalisation and mergers and acquisitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Strengthening business resilience lies at the heart of the Enterprise Financing Scheme, which has been enhanced to provide SMEs with better access to funding and working capital support for internationalisation and mergers and acquisitions.

sections.label: Private Credit Growth Fund and Enterprise Compute Initiative
sections.summary: The Private Credit Growth Fund offers alternative financing to businesses in emerging and high-growth sectors, while the Enterprise Compute Initiative gives SMEs and startups access to computational resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The newly established Private Credit Growth Fund will provide alternative financing options to businesses, particularly in emerging and high-growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This fund is an essential step in enhancing Singapore's financial ecosystem, allowing companies to secure capital from diversified sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Enterprise Compute Initiative will play a crucial role in equipping our businesses, especially our SMEs and startups, with greater access to computational resources, ensuring they can harness artificial intelligence and high-performance computing to stay competitive.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme improvement
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Credit Scheme has been improved to give employers higher co-funding support for fair wages and career progression for lower-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Credit Scheme has been further improved, providing employers with higher co-funding support to encourage fair wages and career progression for lower-income workers.

sections.label: Fiscal prudence and surplus
sections.summary: Continued fiscal prudence has allowed Singapore to maintain a surplus, reflecting the Government's commitment to long-term financial stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our nation's continued fiscal prudence has allowed Singapore to maintain a surplus, reflecting the Government's commitment to long-term financial stability.

sections.label: CDC and GST vouchers continuation
sections.summary: The continuation of CDC Vouchers and GST vouchers will be appreciated, especially by lower-income families who look forward to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, the continuation of the CDC Vouchers and GST vouchers will be appreciated, especially by families with lower incomes who look forward to these.

sections.label: SkillsFuture retraining and income allowances
sections.summary: Government assistance for retraining through SkillsFuture and allowances for lost income during retraining act as buffers during disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government’s intervention in providing assistance for retraining through SkillsFuture, as well as, importantly, generous allowances that make up for lost income while people retrain, will be important buffers for people as they cope with this disruption.

sections.label: Budget, SG Cultural Pass, economic figures
sections.summary: Budget sets aside $300 million for SG Cultural Pass, giving $100 to each Singaporean for local arts events, with vouchers redeemable from September 2025 to end-2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this year’s Budget, I note that $300 million is being set aside for the SG Cultural Pass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This translates into $100 to every Singaporean to spend on local arts events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would strongly encourage local groups to consider organising events that can tap on these funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These vouchers can be redeemed from September 2025 to the end of 2028, so there is a good window of time for groups to plan activities. : Mr Deputy Speaker, this is a wide-ranging Budget that provides support that Singaporeans need in a range of areas, including cost of living, employment and having families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore’s economy grew by 4.4% last year against all odds, driven by better-than-expected performance in wholesale trade, finance and insurance, as well as our manufacturing sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, our gross domestic product (GDP) growth is projected to moderate between 1% and 3% in 2025 as global uncertainty and emerging market risks continue to impact our economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, our core inflation rate is expected to ease to an average of 1.5% to 2.5%.

sections.label: Uplifting Employment Credit for ex-offenders
sections.summary: Extending the Uplifting Employment Credit to 2028 is essential for ex-offenders reintegrating into society, having supported nearly 700 employers hiring over 1,000 ex-offenders last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Likewise, extending the Uplifting Employment Credit to 2028 is essential to assist ex-offenders in reintegrating into society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I note that the credit supported nearly 700 employers in hiring over 1,000 ex-offenders last year.

sections.label: Polytechnic graduate employment survey results
sections.summary: Graduate Employment Survey results showed 54.6% of polytechnic graduates were in full-time permanent jobs in 2024, compared with almost 60% in 2023 and 59% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recent results cited in a Straits Times article on 6 February from the Graduate Employment Survey by the five polytechnics in Singapore released on 13 January showed that 54.6% graduates were in full-time permanent jobs in 2024, compared with almost 60% in 2023 and 59% in 2022.

sections.label: Matched MediSave Scheme for seniors
sections.summary: The Matched MediSave Scheme offers dollar-for-dollar matching grants of up to $1,000 annually for lower-income seniors aged 55 to 70, complementing the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Matched MediSave Scheme will offer dollar-for-dollar matching grants of up to $1,000 annually for lower-income seniors aged 55 to 70, complementing the existing Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.

sections.label: MediSave, seniors, and private estate support
sections.summary: Speaker hopes Government considers enhancing MediSave use for seniors' long-term and palliative care, recommends raising the $2,500 lifetime withdrawal limit, and welcomes the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme extension to private properties until 2028.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I hope that the Government would also continue to consider enhancing more use of MediSave funds by seniors and their family members to manage long-drawn commitment to long-term and palliative care costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I recommend increasing the lifetime withdrawal limit for seniors with limited MediSave savings when utilising a family member's MediSave, currently capped at $2,500 per patient to an amount more commensurate to the real cost of such long-term care costs of an average Singaporean senior at the average lifespan that we are enjoying as one of the longest, if not, the longest living people on earth now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I strongly advocated in a PQ in this House last year on providing senior-friendly enhancements under the MND's Estate Upgrading Programme for private estates as seniors ageing in their private homes require similar support as those living in HDB estates, especially if they are asset-rich but cash poor and unwilling to sell a home that they have bought many decades ago and where they have treasured memories of bringing up their children in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am thus extremely delighted to hear that the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme will be extended to also cover private properties for three years until 2028, in addition to HDB flats.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant enhancement
sections.summary: The Home Caregiving Grant enhancement raises the maximum grant to $600 monthly and the qualifying income ceiling to $4,800 per capita.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On this front, I welcome the Home Caregiving Grant enhancement, which increases the maximum grant to $600 monthly and raises the qualifying income ceiling to $4,800 per capita, ensuring more caregivers can receive financial support to defray caregiving costs.

sections.label: Preschool fee caps and Large Families Scheme
sections.summary: Reduced monthly fee caps for Government-supported preschools ease young parents' financial load, and the Large Families Scheme was announced in Budget 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The reduction in the monthly fee caps of Government-supported preschools will go some way in lightening the financial load on young parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I was excited to hear the announcement of the Large Families Scheme by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Finance Minister in his Budget 2025 speech last week.

sections.label: Employment credit and skills support
sections.summary: The enhanced Workfare Skills Support scheme and extended Senior, Enabling and Uplifting Employment Credits help employees upgrade skills and keep jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For working residents, the Government has strengthened support through the enhanced Workfare Skills Support scheme and extended the Senior Employment Credit, the Enabling Employment Credit and the Uplifting Employment Credit to help employees of different ages and backgrounds upgrade their skills and keep their jobs.

sections.label: Corrected 2035 emissions target figure
sections.summary: The correct 2035 emissions reduction commitment figure is between 45 to 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, not 45 to 55 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Just now, in my earlier speech, I said that in Singapore's NDC recent submissions, we had committed to reducing our emissions to between 45 to 55 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: I wish to clarify that the correct figure should be between 45 to 50 million tonnes instead.

sections.label: Inflation slowdown in 2024
sections.summary: Prices rose 3.7% at the start of 2024 but slowed to 1.6% by year end, below MAS' unofficial target of just under 2%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At the brink of 2024, prices were rising at an uncomfortable rate of 3.7%, relative to the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But by the end of last year, this had slowed to 1.6%, lower than the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') unofficial target of just under 2%.

sections.label: Falling annual increase rates
sections.summary: Increases mostly between 3% and 4% in the 2010s fell to 2.3% in 2020, 0.9% in 2021, -1% in 2022 and 0.2% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From increases that were mostly between 3% and 4% in the 2010s, this fell to 2.3% in 2020, 0.9% in 2021, -1% in 2022 and 0.2% in 2023.

sections.label: Real wage growth 2019 to 2024
sections.summary: MOM's own figures show real wages grew only 0.7% between 2019 and 2024, lower than the prior decade's near 3%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: By the MOM's own calculus, real wages grew by only 0.7% between 2019 and 2024, significantly lower than the prior decade where it was closer to 3%.

sections.label: Education professionals' inflation-adjusted wage growth
sections.summary: The speaker calculates education service professionals' wages grew 1.1% annually in inflation-adjusted terms from 2019 to 2024, similar to the 0.7% nationwide increase.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on my calculations, between 2019 and 2024, wages grew, in inflation-adjusted terms, at an average annual rate of 1.1% for this group.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This means that our school teachers and other education service professionals – the ones that we entrust to preside over our children’s learning and development – saw their incomes increase at a rate not much different to the very modest nationwide increase of 0.7%.

sections.label: NWC lower-wage worker increases
sections.summary: The NWC has advocated built-in wage increases of between 5.5% and 7.5% for lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The NWC has advocated for built-in wage increases of between 5.5% and 7.5% for lower-wage workers.

sections.label: NWC one-off wage hike recommendation
sections.summary: With cumulative inflation of around 7% over two years, the speaker says it is justifiable for the NWC to expand recommendations to an across-the-board one-off wage hike of 5.5% to 7.5%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With cumulative inflation over the past two years of around 7%, it is fully justifiable for the NWC to expand its recommendations to an across-the-board, one-off wage hike of between 5.5% and 7.5%.

sections.label: Contribution rates peak and taper
sections.summary: Overall contributions gradually rose to a peak of 50% in 1984 before tapering down to 40% in the late 1990s.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Overall contributions gradually rose to a peak of 50% in 1984 before tapering down to 40% in the late 1990s.

sections.label: CPF monthly ceiling raised
sections.summary: Two Budgets ago, the Government raised the CPF monthly ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Two Budgets ago, the Government raised the CPF monthly ceiling, from $6,000 to $8,000.

sections.label: Minimum wage statutory universal
sections.summary: The speaker notes PM Wong set $1,600 for full-timers and, with nine in 10 low-income workers covered, believes the minimum wage should be statutory and universal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In last year’s Budget speech, Prime Minister Wong set this at $1,600 for full-timers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the coverage of low-income earners by either the minimum wage component of the Progressive Wage Model or the LQS is now nine in 10 workers, I believe that the minimum wage should simply be made statutory and universal.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement payouts increase
sections.summary: The speaker suggests boosting WIS payouts, noting higher payments since January, and asks if payouts can rise with living costs and a higher cash component.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, to help these lower-income workers cope better, we should consider boosting our Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am heartened that since January this year, employees on WIS received higher payments of up to $4,900 per year, with 40% in cash and 60% in CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For the self-employed and platform workers, payouts are up to $3,267 per year with 10% in cash and 90% in MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the payouts be increased to take into account the rise in the cost of living and adjusted to provide a higher cash component?

sections.label: Sale of Balance flats, BTO waiting time
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether more Sale of Balance flats can be set aside and urges MND to build more BTO flats to cut waiting time to 12 to 18 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can a greater number of Sale of Balance flats be set aside for their selection?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge MND to commit more resources to the building of BTO flats to reduce the waiting time to 12 to 18 months.

sections.label: Annual child credits extension
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the annual credits of $1,000 per child could be extended until age 21 or completion of National Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the same time, the annual credits of $1,000 per child can be considered extended until the age of 21 or the completion of National Service.

sections.label: Singapore Blue Zone 2.0
sections.summary: Singapore was declared a Blue Zone 2.0 in August 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Singapore was declared a Blue Zone 2.0 in August 2023.

sections.label: Singapore life expectancy and health span
sections.summary: Singaporeans have an average life expectancy of 84.3 years, men 84 and women 88, with health span at 74.2 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Singaporeans have an average life expectancy of 84.3 years, with men having an average life span of 84 years, while women living to an average of 88 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The health span of Singaporeans, that is, years lived in good health is at 74.2 years.

sections.label: Singapore seniors by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be 65 or older.
