sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four in Singaporeans will be 65 or older.

sections.label: Germany's first pension system
sections.summary: In 1889, Germany introduced the world's first pension system for Germans aged 70 and older.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In 1889, Germany introduced the world's first pension system: giving Germans who were 70 years and older, especially those who could no longer work, financial security in their old age.

sections.label: France retirement age protests
sections.summary: In 2023, France saw widespread protests over raising the retirement age from 62 to 64.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In 2023, France experienced widespread protests raising the retirement age from 62 to 64.

sections.label: Active seniors at retirement age
sections.summary: At retirement age, 64 in Singapore by 2026, many seniors met are still active and able to work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: At retirement age – which in Singapore's context will be 64 by 2026 – many seniors whom I meet are still physically active, cognitively sharp and more than able to be involved in a productive activity, one way or another.

sections.label: Budget schemes and senior employment
sections.summary: Beyond Budget measures like the Matched MediSave Scheme, more can be done on senior employment, amid expected Budget spending.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Beyond the various measures like the Matched MediSave Scheme, the enhanced Home Caregiving Grants and broadening of HDB's Enhancement for Active Seniors programme under this Budget, there is scope for us to do more, to move the needle on senior employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As the volume over the General Elections builds, many expect that the spending taps will be turned on during this year's Budget, and we have certainly seen generous schemes and various vouchers announced across the board, paid for by higher-than-expected corporate tax revenues.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We see the introduction of, for example, the $100 SG Culture Pass, $100 ActiveSG credits, including private property into the Climate Vouchers scheme, hawker centre stall rental rebates, and even LifeSG credits for children under 18.

sections.label: Singaporeans with many specialist appointments
sections.summary: 2019 figures showed over 7,000 Singaporeans yearly attending 24 or more Specialist Outpatient appointments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The 2019 figures from before COVID-19, showed that over 7,000 Singaporeans a year have to attend 24 or more Specialist Outpatient appointments in a calendar year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In that same year, there were over 2,000 Singaporeans who have 36 or more appointments at a Specialist Clinic every year.

sections.label: Care coordination funding and caregivers
sections.summary: Agencies should treat care coordination as an enabler, and Government should fund it holistically, as caregiving burdens fall hardest on vulnerable workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, our agencies need to get better at recognising the amount of work that is needed to coordinate care and then to recognise that care coordination should not be seen as a cost centre and expense in and of itself, but as an enabler and a catalyst to simplify the care journey for a fellow Singaporean in need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I also call upon the Government, and especially MOF, to take a more holistic view of subsidising and funding care coordination, whether it is funding to hire more patient navigators or care navigators, or recognising additional hours put in outside of official duty hours by frontline staff who are working extra hard to coordinate for the patients and those under their care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Furthermore, with smaller family sizes in Singapore today, with fewer children, the caregiving responsibility is heavier for each grown up child and it is the most vulnerable workers who are hit hardest, workers who cannot do their work remotely, who cannot log in through Zoom or video conference, workers who have less bargaining power at the workplace, workers who might be daily-rated and for whom every half-day or every day taken out of work to care and support their family member, means a day in lost income, a day of economic impact.

sections.label: Digital dropout definition
sections.summary: Digital dropout is when someone stops using a Government service because it went digital and they can no longer access it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Digital dropout happens when someone who used to make use of a Government service no longer uses the service anymore because it went digital – not because their problems have gone away, but because they can no longer get to the service or find it so hard that they have given up trying to access the service.

sections.label: Pro-Citizen Process Review proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an IMC on Pro-Citizen Process Review, or BOSS, chaired by a senior Cabinet Minister, to simplify Government processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If helping our SMEs is important enough to have a Deputy Prime Minister chairing an IMC, then I suggest, Mr Speaker, we should adopt the same approach to helping our fellow Singaporeans, our fellow citizens navigate Government processes too and look at ways to make it as simple as possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I call upon the Government: if we have an IMC on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review, we can also have an IMC on Pro-Citizen Process Review – or what we can call the Bureau Of Services Simplification; we can call it "BOSS".

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It can be chaired by a senior Cabinet Minister at the Deputy Prime Minister or Senior Minister level, supported by younger officeholders and an advisory panel of public and private sector experts who understand user experience and user design, seeing through the eyes of our people, not just the eyes of engineers or coders, however they mean well; seeing through the eyes of a senior, who cannot go online to book an offline appointment in the real world with an agency; seeing through the eyes of patients and caregivers, who may be struggling to navigate the complexity of multiple apps, multiple platforms; seeing through the eyes of a young Clementi couple where hubby had to give up his work to bring his wife to the polyclinic every day because the system could not bring subsidised care to the home in the same way.

sections.label: Quantum computing on a chip
sections.summary: Microsoft announced a new platform to have quantum computers on a chip, showing technology moves quickly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Just last week, Microsoft announced a new platform to have quantum computers on a chip.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, the take-home message is: technology is moving quickly, and what we think may be hypothetical questions seven years ago are real questions applicable today.

sections.label: AI for the people
sections.summary: The biggest AI gains will come when AI connects to real-world work, and MOE must ensure every child learns AI.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The biggest gains from AI will not be virtual.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It will be when AI connects to the real world, when AI connects, empowers people in the real world doing real-world work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It must be AI for the people, regardless of your social economic background, regardless of what you are doing, regardless of whether you are born to a tech-savvy family with lots of Internet access who can pay for the latest models, or whether you are growing up starting with less.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And therefore, MOE needs to ensure every child gets the chance to learn AI, at a pace they are comfortable with and have access to good quality AI models.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Access to the best AI models should not just be for the child who is born to a wealthy tech-savvy family.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It must also be AI not just for big businesses with deep pockets, but also small companies or SMEs.

sections.label: AI for home-based businesses
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the new Enterprise Compute Initiative will cover home-based businesses, noting benefits across Government and society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: But if one of the stronger commercial AI models can someday run on her smartphone, be a virtual manager or chief operating officer, that will empower her, allow her real world skills to have more of an impact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: So, can MOF confirm whether the new Enterprise Compute Initiative will cover home-based businesses?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: If by spending a bit more to help caregivers, we save someone's job, we must look at the benefits across Government and society.

sections.label: COVID support schemes for Singaporeans
sections.summary: COVID initiatives like the Jobs Support Scheme, Wage Credit Scheme, SGUnited Traineeship and CDC Vouchers provided relief to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: COVID initiatives, probably forgotten by some by now, like the Jobs Support Scheme, Wage Credit Scheme, the SGUnited Traineeship, CDC Vouchers, first started to help the hawkers, to name a few, have provided much-needed relief to Singaporeans.

sections.label: DBS job cuts and new positions
sections.summary: DBS Group announced plans to cut 4,000 jobs over three years while adding 1,000 new positions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For instance, the DBS Group recently announced plans to cut 4,000 jobs over the next three years while, of course, adding 1,000 new positions.

sections.label: Budget 2025 SkillsFuture enhancements
sections.summary: Budget 2025 initiatives enhance the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for mid-career Singaporeans, adding part-time courses and employer incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Budget 2025 initiatives like enhancing the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for mid-career Singaporeans, adding part-time courses and enhancing employer incentives are commendable.

sections.label: DBS AI job cuts and reskilling
sections.summary: DBS announced job cuts due to AI applications and will send 13,000 staff for AI and data upskilling or reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The recent DBS announcements of job cut this week due to AI applications and the decision therefore to send 13,000 staff to be upskilled or reskilled in AI and data, is another clarion call for us for urgent action.

sections.label: Campaigns for lifelong learning
sections.summary: The passage calls for allocating resources and developing campaigns to compel Singaporeans to take lifelong learning seriously and self-drive their development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Let us allocate resources and develop campaigns to compel Singaporeans to take lifelong learning seriously and to proactively self-drive our own developments.

sections.label: Upskilling necessity in AI era
sections.summary: In the AI era and job displacement, upskilling is a critical necessity for retaining jobs and navigating social environments, daily lives and the evolving world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In this era of AI and job displacement, upskilling has become a critical necessity – essential not only for retaining our jobs but also for navigating our social environments, daily lives and the rapidly evolving world around us.

sections.label: Heritage business operating costs
sections.summary: The passage notes the high cost of running a heritage business and a new inter-Ministry task force to support such businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It grapples with the high cost of operating a heritage business in a popular historical district.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But I am encouraged that Minister Desmond Lee of MND has established a new inter-Ministry task force to support the growth and sustainability of heritage businesses like Wardah Books in Singapore’s historic precincts.

sections.label: Focused task forces for challenges
sections.summary: The passage proposes establishing focused task forces to investigate root causes and develop solutions, seeking policy exceptions if needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To address these challenges effectively, we should really establish focused task forces to conduct deep-dive exercises to investigate the root causes of their challenges, their profiles and develop creative and practical solutions and seek Government policy exceptions if needed.

sections.label: Volunteer support for families
sections.summary: For three years volunteers provided home visits, activities, legal talks and services, funded by a sponsor for a coordinator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For three years, this group of volunteers have provided home visits, organised activities, invited them to grassroots activities, community activities, organised legal talks to help them, pushed out legal services to support them and fostered a sense of community, reminding these families that they are not alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, this initiative was only possible due to a team of passionate grassroots volunteers and a generous sponsor that I found who co-funded the central coordination person, headcount.

sections.label: Government facilitating community solutions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Government could play a part in facilitating community-driven solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could Government play a part in facilitating these community-driven solutions?

sections.label: Three areas for Government
sections.summary: The passage summarises three areas for Government: upskilling and job transformation, safeguarding vulnerable groups and businesses, and enabling community-driven solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In summary, Sir, I have brought up three areas for Government to further deep dive into: one, accelerating upskilling and job transformation in the age of AI; two, better safeguard the vulnerable groups and businesses; and three, empowering and facilitating more community-driven solutions for skill and for more lives to be impacted.

sections.label: Giraffe, strength, Budget surplus
sections.summary: The passage cites the giraffe, national strength, the Prime Minister's remarks, and a Budget surplus of $6.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The giraffe reminds us that progress is not just about individual success but also about lifting others as we climb.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We, in Singapore, are only as strong as our weakest member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In his opening remarks, the Prime Minister reminded all of us that, "Singapore today is far stronger than we were 60 years ago." For us to enjoy an expected Budget surplus of $6.8 billion, or 0.9% of GDP in 2025, and a similar figure in 2024, especially when we are a country without natural resources is not something to take for granted.

sections.label: Empowering Persons with Disabilities focus
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes this year's focus on empowering persons with disabilities and the Prime Minister's recognition of post-18 concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this spirit, I fully welcome the dedicated focus on "Empowering Persons with Disabilities" this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am also very heartened to hear the Prime Minister specifically recognising the concerns in the post-18 space and I look forward to hearing more about the initiatives that will be shared by MOE and MSF during the COS debates.

sections.label: Coldplay concert deaf zone
sections.summary: A Coldplay concert in January last year had a special zone for fans who are deaf or hard of hearing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another heartwarming example was the Coldplay concert in January last year that had a special zone for fans who are deaf or hard of hearing.

sections.label: SG Culture Pass credits
sections.summary: Prime Minister Wong introduced the SG Culture Pass, giving every Singaporean aged 18 and above $100 credits for arts and heritage events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the Budget speech, Prime Minister Wong introduced the SG Culture Pass, granting every Singaporean aged 18 and above, $100 credits to attend arts and heritage events.

sections.label: Refreshed Disability Sports Master Plan
sections.summary: MCCY announced the refreshed Disability Sports Master Plan 2024, which identified three strategic themes for disability sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) announced the refreshed Disability Sports Master Plan (DSMP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: DSMP 2024 identified three strategic themes: one, increasing accessibility to disability sports activities and programmes; two, enhancing awareness of disability sports and inclusive sports activities; and three, fulfilling high performance aspirations of persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Disability Sports Master Plan name
sections.summary: The speaker says the name Disability Sports Master Plan risks creating the perception that the plan is only for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the current name "Disability Sports Master Plan" is well-intended to put the spotlight on promoting disability sports at a recreational and high performance level, it risks creating the perception that this plan is only for persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Strategic Moves 4 and 5
sections.summary: Strategic Move 4 aims for all mainstream schools to offer disability sports by 2028, and Strategic Move 5 expands Play Inclusive outreach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, I found Strategic Move 4 very encouraging, as we aim to have all mainstream schools offer opportunities for students to experience disability sports by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another positive initiative comes under Strategic Move 5, which is to increase the outreach of Play Inclusive, a unified sports competition where students from SPED and mainstream schools train and compete together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In order to qualify, unified teams have to train together in the respective sports for a minimum of eight weeks.

sections.label: Aquatic Centre wheelchair counter closed
sections.summary: The Aquatic Centre has a wheelchair accessible ticket counter that the speaker says is always closed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, while the Aquatic Centre does have a wheelchair accessible counter for ticket purchase, it is unfortunately always closed in my personal experience.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)

sentences.text: To address these issues, we must implement targeted and ongoing policies that address the underlying social, economic, political and cultural factors that assist to create and perpetuate gender inequality.

sentences.text: This Budget takes steps in the right direction – the Home Caregiving Grant increase and the extension of the Senior Employment Credit are welcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I propose a Special Lift Retrofit Fund to explore compact lift solutions for blocks without direct lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The super-aged society is not a distant future – it is already here.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Enhancing childcare leave specifically would significantly help parents manage these unpredictable and often stressful situations.

sentences.text: Moving on to the SG Culture Pass, which will provide all Singaporeans aged 18 and above with $100 worth of credits for activities like arts and cultural performances, museum exhibitions and heritage experiences.

sections.label: Reviewing seven days annual leave

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2023, the average number of paid annual leave for full-time employees earning below $2,000 was 12 days, compared to 17 days for those earning between $2,000 and $4,999 and 21 days for those earning $5,000 and above. 12 days seems low, but even that would be a blessing for 8% of full-time resident employees who receive the very minimum of seven days.

sections.label: Higher minimum leave elsewhere

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More than 160 countries already provide a higher minimum annual leave entitlement.

sentences.text: I know we are also concerned about business costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But when we consider that 90% of our workforce already have more than seven days of annual leave, increasing this minimum entitlement will not significantly cost businesses much more.

sentences.text: But for the individual worker, it is hugely significant as additional time for rest and for spending time with their loved ones.

sentences.text: We took a supported, phased and gradual approach when we doubled and mandated paternity leave entitlements.

sentences.text: Along with the handouts that we will give out to help Singaporeans with the cost of living, I sincerely hope that we will finally increase our minimum annual leave entitlement after 57 years, to help Singaporeans have the time for living.

sentences.text: As a result, I believe the Government will need to subsidise the cost of putting Singaporeans in the global job rotation programmes.

sections.label: Tech@SG Programme support
sections.summary: The Tech@SG Programme, a joint initiative by EDB and Enterprise Singapore, helps fast-growing local companies and SMEs access critical talent.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Tech@SG Programme, a joint initiative by EDB and Enterprise Singapore, supports this balanced approach, helping both the fast-growing local companies and SMEs to access critical talent.

sections.label: Employment Pass quotas and skills transfer
sections.summary: The passage proposes separate Employment Pass quotas for MNCs and SMEs, higher minimum salaries for MNCs hiring junior foreign professionals, and skills transfer programmes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Implement separate Employment Pass quotas for MNCs and SMEs, with a more generous quota towards our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Increase the minimum qualifying salary for MNCs to hire foreign professionals in junior roles.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Encourage MNCs to implement skills transfer programmes where they are required to train local employees to take on senior roles gradually.

sections.label: Earlier ITE enrolment for students
sections.summary: The speaker notes over 9,000 youths sit the N level examinations yearly and asks whether non-academically inclined students could enrol in ITE at 13.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Next, about harnessing and broadening our talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: I would say, each year, over 9,000 youths sit for the “N” level examinations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Have we considered to allow students who are not academically inclined to enrol in ITE much earlier, say, at the age of 13?

sections.label: Broadening definition of success
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to broaden the definition of success and give Singaporeans more career pathway choices.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With a healthier and happier workforce, we too look towards a more harmonious and prosperous society.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to take a vital step towards broadening our definition of success and how Singaporeans can have more choices in their career pathway, as we join hands to ensure Singapore’s continued success on the global stage.

sections.label: Expanding National Research Fund fields
sections.summary: Speaker appeals to Government to expand National Research Fund fields to non-science, non-tech areas with broad societal applicability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And I share Deputy Prime Minister Heng's concern about how, in many administrations around the world, this has been slashed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That said, if I may appeal to the Government, when it comes to projects to be funded by the National Research Fund going forward, if we could expand the fields of inquiry to also non-science, non-tech areas, so long as these have a broad societal applicability.

sections.label: Multiple research funding pots
sections.summary: Speaker states there are many different pots of research funding for different activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As for his specific inquiry, actually, we have many different pots of research funding for different activities.

sections.label: Research panels and Social Sciences group
sections.summary: Speaker notes research panels assess proposal quality and a Social Sciences and Humanities Research Group was created a few years back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have our research panels that look at the quality of these proposals as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have also recently, a few years back, created the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Group that will look at the research in this area.

sections.label: Funding research with practical applications
sections.summary: Speaker says much funding goes to sciences, with scope for research translating into practices and immediate improvements, citing healthy longevity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We do fund a lot of that, particularly in the sciences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But there is also a lot of scope for us to fund and do research that can be translated into actual practices, into seeing immediate improvements in the lives of people, whether it is in healthcare, and that is why I mentioned one of the big challenges that we are working on is healthy longevity.

sections.label: Succession planning and leadership support
sections.summary: Speaker says succession planning ensures continuity, expresses appreciation to Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong and support for Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and 4G team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our careful, deliberate succession planning ensures continuity in governance, preserving our progress while allowing for a necessary evolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We express our deepest appreciation to Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong for his decades of steadfast leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We also extend our full support for Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and the 4G leadership team as they take on the responsibility of steering Singapore into the future.

sections.label: Budget investments and Changi Airport Fund
sections.summary: Speaker says Budget continues investments in competitiveness, workforce upskilling, innovation, AI and infrastructure, with $5 billion more for Changi Airport Development Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Budget continues our investments in enhancing our global competitiveness, ensuring Singapore remains a top destination for businesses and investors, upskilling our workforce with the skills of tomorrow, investing in innovation and technology, especially in AI, which was explained in great detail by Deputy Prime Minister Heng, and investment in infrastructure to support long-term growth, in particular, the Changi Airport Development Fund and Future Energy Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Budget sets aside an additional $5 billion for the Changi Airport Development Fund, reinforcing the importance of our ports and airports as strategic national assets.

sections.label: Air hub and energy fund
sections.summary: The passage asks about a long-term roadmap for Singapore's air hub competitiveness and notes a $5 billion top-up for the Future Energy Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What is the Government's long-term roadmap to integrate these elements and ensure Singapore's air hub competitiveness is sustained into the future?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Budget also allocates a $5 billion top-up for the Future Energy Fund, reinforcing our commitment to securing a low-carbon, sustainable and safe energy future.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant increase
sections.summary: The speaker called for a higher Home Caregiving Grant, which has risen from $200 to $400 and now $600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I called for a further increase in the Home Caregiving Grant to better support caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am glad that since then, the grant has been raised from $200 to $400, and now to $600, providing much needed relief for caregivers like Mdm Neo.

sections.label: Seniors, ComCare and PwDs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether ComCare eligibility should be lowered for asset-less seniors and notes the Enabling Employment Credit extension to 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While the Lease Buyback Scheme is an option for senior homeowners, should we lower ComCare eligibility requirements for seniors with no assets, especially those whose children are also struggling financially?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On persons with disabilities (PwDs), extending the Enabling Employment Credit to 2028 helps offset hiring cost.

sections.label: GST and green investment tax
sections.summary: The speaker urges liberalising GST input tax claims on carbon credit trading and exempting overseas qualifying green investment gains from corporate tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To this end, I urge the Government to liberalise the GST treatment for input tax claims on carbon credit trading-related expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Additionally, I propose that gains derived from qualifying green investments made by Singaporean investors overseas be exempted from corporate tax, similar to the foreign-sourced dividends exemption.

sections.label: COEs for commercial vans
sections.summary: The speaker suggests channeling additional COE supply to commercial vans to lower SME operating costs and benefit end users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, to ease the financial burden on SMEs, I suggest channeling the additional supply of Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) towards commercial vans, which will help lower operating costs and, ultimately, benefit end users.

sections.label: Land use and wage support
sections.summary: The passage notes temporary land use amendments and car park charge adjustments, and commends 20% wage support for low-earning workers with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I understand this requires temporary land use amendments and adjustments to car park charges, but with the right policy intent, I am confident the Government can resolve these challenges creatively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I commend the Government for introducing 20% wage support for workers with disabilities earning below $4,000 per month.

sections.label: Tax deductions and co-funding
sections.summary: The speaker proposes tax deductions or co-funding with a two-to-three-year window and welcomes the 2024 Partnerships for Capability Transformation expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I propose further tax deductions or co-funding mechanisms, with a limited implementation window of two to three years to assess effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also welcome the Government’s expansion of the Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme in 2024, which fosters deeper collaboration between MNCs and SMEs.

sections.label: Inclusive hiring incentives proposed
sections.summary: The speaker proposes tax rebates, higher foreign worker quotas and bonus points for inclusive employers, and commends 20% wage support for workers with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I understand that this requires temporary land use amendments and adjustments to car park charges, but with the right policy intent, I am confident the Government can resolve these challenges creatively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I commend the Government for introducing 20% wage support for workers with disabilities earning below $4,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To further incentivise employers, I propose: (a) tax rebates for businesses that adopt inclusive hiring practices; (b) higher foreign worker quotas for companies hiring persons with disabilities; and (c) bonus points for inclusive companies in Government project bids.

sections.label: SkillsFuture course recommendations
sections.summary: SkillsFuture can pre-qualify Singaporeans using household income, education and occupation data and directly recommend accredited courses tailored to their needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Since the Government has household data on income, education and occupation, SkillsFuture can pre-qualify Singaporeans and directly recommend accredited courses tailored to their needs.

sections.label: Budget surplus and seized sums
sections.summary: The Budget reports a $6.4 billion surplus, with about $3 billion confiscated from a money laundering syndicate and $6 billion seized from 2019 to June 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Budget Statement reports a surplus of $6.4 billion for this financial year (FY), which the Prime Minister attributes to better-than-expected corporate tax collection.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We also acknowledge the Government's commendable efforts in confiscating approximately $3 billion from a money laundering syndicate last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, a significant sum of $6 billion was seized between January 2019 and June 2024, linked to criminal and money laundering activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While the return of $416 million to the victims and the forfeiture of $1 billion to the state are positive steps, it is understood that a substantial portion remains tied up in ongoing investigations and court proceedings.

sections.label: Canberra floor parties since 2008
sections.summary: In Canberra division of Sembawang GRC, small-scale floor parties have been organised since 2008 so neighbours on the same floor connect over food and drinks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the Canberra division of Sembawang GRC, we have been working to address this challenge since 2008 by organising small-scale "floor parties".

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These gatherings encourage neighbours on the same floor to connect over simple food and drinks in their own shared lobby or corridor.

sections.label: Climate Vouchers for energy efficiency
sections.summary: The initiative provides Climate Vouchers to all households, including private property owners, for buying energy-efficient appliances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The recent initiative to enhance energy efficiency by providing Climate Vouchers to all households, including private property owners, for the purchase of energy-efficient appliances is a commendable step.

sections.label: Canberra recycling bin pilot project
sections.summary: Canberra was offered as a pilot project to the then-Ministry of Environment for one recycling bin per block.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Canberra was even offered as a pilot project to the then-Ministry of Environment to implement one recycling bin per block.

sections.label: Revised FY2024 revenue surplus figures
sections.summary: Revised figures showed an $8 billion rise in operating revenues, which Lawrence Wong attributed mainly to higher corporate income tax, COE and GST collections.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the previous Budget Statement, the Government projected a modest surplus of $0.78 billion for FY2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, revised figures revealed an $8 billion increase in total operating revenues, rising from the estimated $108.6 billion to $116.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong attributed this unexpected revenue surge primarily to a higher corporate income tax collection, which only accounts for less than $3 billion of the increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The remaining $5 billion plus over collections include significant rises in vehicle quota premiums or COEs at nearly $1.9 billion more, and GST at $1.2 billion more.

sections.label: DBS study on retiree CPF reliance
sections.summary: A DBS Bank study of two million customers found retirees aged 65 and above rely on CPF funds for 55% of median expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a DBS Bank study released this month on two million of its customers, retirees aged 65 and above were found to rely on CPF funds to cover 55% of their median expenses.

sections.label: CPF share for non-working spouses
sections.summary: Courts can award a non-working spouse a significant share of the working spouse's CPF, and this justifies protections for non-working spouses remaining in marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Courts are empowered to award a non-working spouse a significant share of the working spouse's CPF balances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The principle here is that the working spouse was only able to concentrate on work because the other spouse focused on attending to the family at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, if a spouse's position is recognised in a divorce, it is all the more justified to consider protections for the non-working spouses who remain in the marriage until their partner's death.

sections.label: Default 50% CPF allocation proposal
sections.summary: Without consent, a default provision could allocate 50% of CPF balances to the spouse, with the member's nomination covering the remaining half.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In cases where consent is not obtained, a default provision could allocate 50% of the CPF balances to the spouse, with the member's nomination applying to the remaining half.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These measures will help households for now, but the issue is how sustainable such an approach is.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe it is vital to seriously look at the three areas I have highlighted: doing better at Budget marksmanship; managing the cost of living other than through handouts; and providing vulnerable segments of society who risk being overlooked in our nation's progress.

sections.label: Zhenghua aid for resource-low families
sections.summary: Zhenghua launched monthly $1 Deals and Project Sama Sama so resource-low families can access essential food and daily necessities affordably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Resource-low families are making difficult trade-offs to make ends meet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That is why we took decisive action, launching Zhenghua's monthly $1 Deals and Project Sama Sama, ensuring families, especially those who are resource-low, can access essential food and daily necessities affordably and conveniently.

sections.label: Preschool fee caps affordability
sections.summary: Capping preschool fees for Anchor and Partner Operators makes early education more affordable, with fees after subsidies comparable to primary school fees including after-school care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By capping preschool fees for Anchor and Partner Operators, early education has now become more affordable, with fees after subsidies being comparable to primary school fees, inclusive of after-school care.

sections.label: Funding for Anchor Operator wages
sections.summary: It asks how the Government will adjust funding for Anchor Operators to ensure preschool teachers get fair wages and resources for professional development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given the fee caps, how will the Government adjust funding for Anchor Operators to ensure that preschool teachers are paid fair wages and have adequate resources for professional development?

sections.label: ESOP tax relief proposal
sections.summary: It proposes introducing an ESOP tax relief, such as a lower income tax rate when employees exercise their stock options, to promote ESOP adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To promote ESOP adoption, we should introduce an ESOP tax relief, such as a lower income tax rate when employees exercise their stock options.

sections.label: Strengthening SMEs employing workforce
sections.summary: It states that SMEs must be strengthened, as they employ over 70% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, we must strengthen SMEs, which employ over 70% of our workforce.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit Scheme changes
sections.summary: Changes to the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit Scheme give employers an online wallet with credits to offset training costs, addressing cash flow and being widely welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The changes to the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit Scheme, where employers are provided with an online wallet with credits to offset training costs, are widely welcomed by employers as they address a common pain point – cash flow.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrator initiative
sections.summary: The Jobs-Skills Integrator (JSIT) initiative was announced in Budget 2023 and is described as another critical piece of the jigsaw puzzle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Jobs-Skills Integrator (JSIT) initiative, announced in Budget 2023, is another critical piece of the jigsaw puzzle.

sections.label: Enterprise Compute Initiative and AI adoption
sections.summary: The passage asks about resource limits in scaling the $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative and programmes helping SMEs adopt AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The newly minted $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative that will empower enterprises with AI tools and resources will certainly be a game-changer in bolstering enterprise capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given the importance of AI adoption among enterprises, I would like to ask the Government what are the current resource limitations in scaling up the Enterprise Compute Initiative so that more enterprises can accelerate AI customisations and adoption?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Particularly for SMEs, what programmes are available to help them leverage AI tools?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By empowering local enterprises to maximise the usage of AI tools, this will improve the overall firm’s productivity which translates to sustained real wage growth for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I propose that we strengthen collaboration between industries and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) by co-locating R&D offices on campuses.

sections.label: Industry-IHL partnerships and commercialisation
sections.summary: Adapting these models can strengthen industry-IHL partnerships, expand co-location and support research commercialisation for enterprise transformation and job creation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By adapting these models, Singapore can strengthen industry-IHL partnerships, expand co-location efforts, and provide greater support for research commercialisation to drive enterprise transformation, economic growth and high-quality job creation for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Special transfers distributed this year
sections.summary: About $3.8 billion of special transfers will be distributed this year, compared to about $3 billion in 2023 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, about $3.8 billion of special transfers will be distributed this year, compared to about $3 billion in both 2023 and 2024.

sections.label: Revenue above original estimates
sections.summary: The Government collected about $8 billion more revenue each year than its original estimates in 2022, 2023 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government has collected about $8 billion more revenue each year than its original estimates in 2022, 2023, and 2024.

sections.label: About $20 billion parked away
sections.summary: The same thing has happened this year, with about $20 billion parked away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The same thing has happened this year, with about $20 billion parked away.

sections.label: Reserves taken out during COVID-19
sections.summary: The $40 billion taken out during COVID-19 has been more than recovered, with official foreign reserves rising over $200 billion since 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Ms Tin Pei Ling suggested yesterday that we should put back into the Reserves what was taken out during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: She may not realise, but the $40 billion that was taken out has already been more than recovered, with the official foreign reserves increasing more than $200 billion since 2020, through the issuance of Reserves Management Government securities.

sections.label: NIRC and Budget resources
sections.summary: The NIRC amounts to about $27 billion in 2025, but about 80% of Budget resources from it is parked in endowment and trust funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The NIRC amounts to about $27 billion in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, as I have explained before, Budget resources amounting to about 80% of the NIRC is not spent in the same year but parked in endowment and trust funds.

sections.label: Gross minimum living wage proposal
sections.summary: The third proposal is to introduce a gross minimum living wage of $2,250 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our third proposal is to introduce a gross minimum living wage of $2,250 a month.

sections.label: Caregiving Allowance Scheme payments
sections.summary: The Caregiving Allowance Scheme will pay one parent or grandparent $1,250 per month if they are full-time caregivers of children below seven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Caregiving Allowance Scheme will pay one parent or grandparent an allowance of $1,250 per month if they are full-time caregivers of children below the age of seven.

sections.label: Vision for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker rejects a Singapore where elites and foreign billionaires enjoy luxuries while the elderly and destitute sell tissue paper, and wants Singaporeans free of financial stress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We do not want a first-world Singapore where a small group of elites and foreign billionaires coming here to pay lower taxes get to enjoy large Good Class Bungalows, play golf at country clubs and drive around on congestion-free roads in their Bentleys and Lamborghinis while the elderly and destitute sell tissue paper at hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We want a Singapore where Singaporeans are no longer financially stressed, can form families when they are ready, are free to pursue their careers and start businesses, are free from worries about healthcare and retirement cost, and enjoy a fulfilling retirement life, looking after their grandchildren as a choice.

sections.label: PSP support for Budget 2025
sections.summary: Despite reservations, PSP will support Budget 2025 to provide Singaporeans short-term assistance until long-term schemes are in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding our reservations, PSP will still support Budget 2025 to provide Singaporeans with the short-term assistance that they need until the long-term schemes are in place.

sections.label: Competitiveness and family support
sections.summary: The Budget bolsters Singapore's competitiveness through research, innovation and workforce training, and the speaker welcomes the Large Family Scheme and LifeSG credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: First, it bolsters Singapore's competitiveness by funnelling resources into research, innovation and workforce training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, particularly heartened by the Large Family Scheme and the LifeSG credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: These extend added financial support to families with three or more young children.

sections.label: Little Steps KidSTART families grant
sections.summary: North West CDC's Little Steps programme gives KidSTART families $500 yearly per child aged zero to six, disbursing nearly $1.3 million to 2,069 children since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In North West CDC, for instance, the Little Steps programme has been a lifeline for our KidSTART families since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It provides an annual grant of $500 for each child aged between zero and six years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have disbursed close to $1.3 million to help 2,069 children in the district since its launch.

sections.label: Equalising childcare grants for mothers
sections.summary: The passage proposes equalising childcare grants so the same subsidy level applies whether a mother is employed or stays home to care for her children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For example, to equalise childcare grants, ensuring that the same level of subsidy, whether a mother is employed or has chosen to remain at home for a season, to dedicate time to caring for their children.

sections.label: Budget goals and tough choices
sections.summary: The passage states Budget goals go beyond rhetoric and require steadfast action for Singapore's long-term future, even politically tough choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: When we debate this Budget, we must not forget that our goals go beyond mere rhetoric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We must remain steadfast in doing what is necessary for Singapore’s long-term future, whether it is bolstering social support, investing in innovation or ensuring long-term fiscal sustainability, even if the path demands politically tough choices.

sections.label: Unity, SG60 Budget, fiscal position
sections.summary: The passage calls for unity and confidence in the SG60 Budget, and notes Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's estimate of a $0.78 billion overall fiscal position for FY2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Our unwavering sense of togetherness is the shield that keeps us safe and the compass that guides our progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, may this Budget embolden every Singaporean to look ahead with confidence in this SG60 year, knowing that this Government is committed to uplifting lives, supporting our families and safeguarding our sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Let us carry that same spirit into this next chapter, forging a future where Singapore remains a beacon of possibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So long as we stand united, we will prevail – just as we have done for six remarkable decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In September 2024, I asked for an update on the current cumulative fiscal position of the current term of Government, where Prime Minister Lawrence Wong shared that FY2024 is still ongoing, but the overall fiscal position is estimated to be $0.78 billion.

sections.label: Singapore accounting and land sale proceeds
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's accounting differs from IMF norms, notably excluding land sale proceeds of $25 billion in FY2024 and an estimated $19.4 billion in FY2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In fact, it is closer to $72 billion over the last four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And let us also not forget that Singapore's way of accounting differs from international norms, such as that of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the most notable of which is the exclusion of land sale proceeds amounting to $25 billion in FY2024 and estimated at $19.4 billion in FY2025.

sections.label: FY2023 deficit and Majulah Package Fund
sections.summary: The passage states FY2023 recorded a $2.5 billion deficit after setting aside an additional $7.5 billion for the Majulah Package Fund, without which it would have been a $5 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: FY2023 estimated to record a deficit of $0.4 billion and although the deficit was wider than expected at $2.5 billion, this was after setting aside an additional $7.5 billion for the Majulah Package Fund, without which, FY2023 would have seen a $5 billion surplus instead.

sections.label: Personal income tax rebate
sections.summary: A tax rebate of 60% of tax payable, up to $200, was introduced in YA 2025, similar to YA 2024 and YA2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On personal income tax, I note the tax rebate worth 60% of tax payable, or up to $200, was introduced in Year of Assessment (YA) 2025, similar to YA 2024, where it was 50% of tax payable, but capped at $200, and also in YA2019.

sections.label: Retiree savings requirement example
sections.summary: A retiree with a conservative lifestyle spending $1,600 monthly would need about $550,000 in savings by retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, a retiree who has a conservative lifestyle with a monthly expense of $1,600 would require approximately $550,000 in savings by retirement.

sections.label: Retirement readiness and CPF balances
sections.summary: A 2024 OCBC survey found 35% of Singaporeans on track with retirement plans, and 52% of CPF members have at least $60,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to a 2024 Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited (OCBC) survey, only 35% of the Singaporeans surveyed were on track with their retirement plans, while only 60% of respondents were working on their retirement plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a recent Parliamentary reply, the Manpower Minister also noted that 52% of all CPF members have at least $60,000 across their combined CPF balances.

sections.label: CPF investment returns and NIRC
sections.summary: Endowas advertised 7.99% potential yearly returns from 2014 to 2024 versus 2.5% in the CPF Ordinary Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Had we implemented such a scheme back then, for example, Endowas, an investment advisory firm, which is approved under the CPF investment scheme, highlighted in an advertisement that from 2014 to 2024, "We are looking at 7.99% potential returns yearly for an 80:20 equities and bonds portfolio, compared to 2.5% interest earned yearly if left invested in the CPF Ordinary Account." Third, if the Government is not confident that our investment entities, be it Temasek or the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC), can over the long term produce better risk adjusted returns that are better than CPF returns, then we are in serious trouble, and the NIRC framework ought to be thoroughly re-examined.

sections.label: Low-income households estimates
sections.summary: Excluding households with no employed persons, an estimated 17,600 households earn under $1,000 monthly, 61,500 earn $1,000 to $1,999, and 57,100 earn $2,000 to $2,999.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Putting aside households with no employed persons, as this could include retirees, there continues to be an estimated 17,600 households earning less than $1,000 a month, 61,500 households earning $1,000 to $1,999 per month, and 57,100 households earning between $2,000 and $2,999 per month.

sections.label: Highest income group growth
sections.summary: Households earning $20,000 and over saw the largest increase, jumping by close to 158,000 from 2014 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: When we break down this growth by monthly household employment income, the household income group that saw the largest increase over the same period is those earning $20,000 and over, jumping by close to 158,000 households from 2014 to 2024, far surpassing any other income group.

sections.label: Singapore wealth inequality growth
sections.summary: A 2024 UBS report found Singapore had the highest wealth inequality growth among 29 major countries from 2008 to 2023, rising nearly 23%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on the UBS report from 2024, across 29 major countries covered by the report, Singapore saw the highest growth in wealth inequality from 2008 to 2023, increasing by nearly 23%.

sections.label: Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme implementation
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme, accepted by the Government in 2016, is expedited for Singaporeans wanting higher returns but lacking financial knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given our rapidly ageing society, this issue will become increasingly important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope we can expedite the implementation of the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme (LRIS), which the Government first accepted in 2016, to allow Singaporeans who desire higher investment returns but lack the financial knowledge to participate.

sections.label: Business tax rebates and SME support
sections.summary: A 50% corporate income tax rebate capped at $40,000, a minimum $2,000 cash payout, the $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative and extended Market Readiness Assistance grant support businesses and SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The 50% corporate income tax rebate, capped at $40,000, provides immediate relief to businesses of all sizes, while the minimum $2,000 cash payout offers crucial cashflow support for smaller enterprises facing cost pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Beyond immediate cost support, the $150 million Enterprise Compute Initiative will help SMEs tap into AI and digital tools, enhancing productivity and competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The extension of the Market Readiness Assistance grant scheme will also support SMEs in expanding overseas, a necessity given our domestic market constraints.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The speaker supports extending the Senior Employment Credit and Enabling Employment Credit to 2026, easing businesses' short-term cost burden and urging them to tap senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses must therefore fully tap into senior workers as a valuable resource.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I strongly support the extension of the Senior Employment Credit and Enabling Employment Credit to 2026, which eases the cost burden for businesses in the short term.

sections.label: SkillsFuture course classification framework
sections.summary: The speaker says the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant can be refined, having proposed to MOE a classification framework with a Mobility Index and Industrial Heat Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant is a step in the right direction, but its implementation can be refined for greater impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, I proposed to MOE the introduction of a classification framework for SkillsFuture courses, featuring a Mobility Index, measuring how well a skill improves career prospects across industry and an Industrial Heat Index, tracking demand in booming sectors.

sections.label: Subsidies for high-demand skills courses
sections.summary: Courses in high-demand future-relevant skills should get higher or full subsidies for worker groups the Government identifies as needing reskilling, including mid-career workers, those in shrinking industries, seniors and PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Courses in such high-demand future relevant skills areas should receive higher subsidies or even full subsidies for specific worker groups that the Government identifies as needing reskilling, such as mid-career workers or those in shrinking industries, as well as seniors or PwDs.

sections.label: Expanding Non-Traditional Sources Occupation List
sections.summary: The Non-Traditional Sources Occupation List is expanded, particularly for manufacturing, to let businesses recruit higher-skilled work permit holders for specialised roles difficult to localise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, expanding the Non-Traditional Sources Occupation List, particularly for the manufacturing sector, to allow businesses to recruit higher-skilled work permit holders for specialised roles that are difficult to localise.

sections.label: Industrial land leases and SME support
sections.summary: The speaker urges extending industrial land lease tenures and flexible renewals, welcomes a $14 billion top-up, and suggests larger firms partner with SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Arising from our AfA report on business competitiveness, I continue to urge the Government to consider extending industrial land lease tenures to better account for the long lead times required for development and amortisation of capital investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, a more flexible lease renewal structure, such as longer renewal periods for businesses investing in productivity or rolling lease extensions for those demonstrating strong economic contributions, could provide companies, especially SMEs, with greater certainty for long-term investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The $14 billion top-up to funds dedicated to productivity, R&D, Changi Airport development and Future Energy is exciting and will help Singapore pull further ahead as a global hub and overcome our energy constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, let us also ensure that our SMEs can benefit from these investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I suggest that larger corporations and Government-linked companies that receive some of these investments be encouraged to partner with SMEs through initiatives like the Partnership for Capability Transformation programme, helping to diffuse capabilities and create opportunities throughout our business ecosystem.

sections.label: Polls on cost-of-living support measures
sections.summary: The speaker notes Bloomberg reported a Milieu Insight poll of 1,002 Singaporeans finding 55% viewed support measures inadequate, worse than 62% the prior year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government itself is cognisant of this; hence, the announcement of measures, such as CDC Vouchers, U-Save rebates and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note with some interest, however, that Bloomberg reported on 22 February 2025 that a poll conducted among 1,002 Singaporeans by Milieu Insight indicated that 55% of respondents viewed these measures as inadequate in helping them cope with the rising cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I know that a similar poll conducted the year before was even worse, with 62% viewing support measures as inadequate.

sections.label: Polytechnic and university graduate employment rates
sections.summary: Graduate Employment Survey results show polytechnic graduate employment fell to 54.6% in 2025 from 60% in 2023, and university graduate employment fell to 79.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In January 2025, the results of a Graduate Employment Survey focusing on graduates from the five local polytechnics were released, indicating an employment rate of 54.6%, down from 60% in 2023 and 59% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The results of a similar survey focused on university graduates showed a fall in employment rates to 79.5% from 84.1% the previous year.

sections.label: Middle class issues highlighted
sections.summary: The speaker says two issues adversely affecting Singapore's middle class were highlighted, hoping for more attention to their plight and worries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have today highlighted two issues which adversely affect the middle class in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope that more attention will be paid to their plight, so that we can better understand their worries and take measures to address them.

sections.label: Wage growth and income inequality
sections.summary: Singaporeans generally saw wage increases outpacing inflation, and income inequality after Government taxes and transfers is at its lowest since 2000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singaporeans generally saw wage increases that outpaced inflation and income inequality after Government taxes and transfers is at its lowest since 2000.

sections.label: Support for larger families
sections.summary: The passage describes pressures on young couples and welcomes government measures including shared parental leave, Child LifeSG Credits and up to $16,000 for third and subsequent children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The pressures of balancing work, childcare and maintaining a home sometimes discourage young couples from expanding their family as they are uncertain if they can provide the same level of support and opportunities for a household with more children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am heartened by the recent steps the Government has taken to ease some of these burdens, such as the move towards shared paid parental leave last year and the introduction of $500 in Child LifeSG Credits for all children aged 12 and below.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The additional support of up to $16,000 for each third and subsequent child, is a welcome measure that recognises the challenges of growing a family in today's economic climate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is strategic in that this scheme is not just for newborns, but for existing families where at least one child is six or younger, and alleviates the dilution of household finances when an additional child arrives towards a more equitable distribution of resources.

sections.label: SkillsFuture framework reboot
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture framework has been rebooted with the Jobseeker Support Scheme and an expanded SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme giving a monthly allowance to mid-career Singaporeans working part-time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture framework as a whole has received a reboot – for example, the Jobseeker Support Scheme announced last year as well as the expansion of the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme targeting mid-career Singaporeans to pursue upskilling, which will now be given a monthly allowance to those who continue to work part-time.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant changes
sections.summary: The speaker supports raising the maximum qualifying per capita household income for the Home Caregiving Grant and increasing its quantum to offset caregiving costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, while it is not quite the full Carer's Allowance, I support the move to raise the maximum qualifying per capita household income for the Home Caregiving Grant as well as the increment of the quantum to offset caregiving costs.

sections.label: Frail and isolated seniors
sections.summary: As of October 2024, Singapore has 64,000 older seniors, 60% frail to severely frail and 4% at high risk of social isolation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of October 2024, Singapore has 64,000 older seniors of whom 60% are frail to severely frail and 4% at high risk of social isolation.

sections.label: Enhancement for Active Seniors
sections.summary: Extending the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme to seniors in older private estates is a good move answering many colleagues' appeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For seniors living in older private estates, extending the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme is a good move and answers the appeal of many of my colleagues and I.

sections.label: Workers' wages and job fears
sections.summary: Two thirds of surveyed workers are satisfied with wages, welfare and work prospects, but one in three fear job losses within three months, with cost of living a top concern.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: On the workers' front, while two thirds of the workers that we surveyed express satisfaction with their wages, welfare and work prospects, one in three also fear job losses within the next three months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Cost of living remains a top concern, with food, healthcare, groceries and utilities ranking as the top four worries in our survey.

sections.label: Union and tripartite dispute cases
sections.summary: CNA reported about 2,000 dispute cases handled by unions in 2022 and 2023, and about 3,000 by the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In that very same article, CNA reported about 2,000 dispute cases that were handled by unions in 2022 and 2023 as well as about 3,000 by the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management in the same period.

sections.label: Future of Jobs skills report
sections.summary: The Future of Jobs report indicates 39% of current skills will evolve or become obsolete within five years, lower than 44% in 2023 and 57% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The latest Future of Jobs report indicates that 39% of our current skills will either evolve or become obsolete within the next five years, which is, thankfully, lower than the 44% in 2023 and 57% in 2020, possibly due to more workers having completed training, reskilling or upskilling measures.

sections.label: AI adoption in large enterprises
sections.summary: IMDA data showed AI adoption among large enterprises in Singapore rose from 16.7% in 2018 to 44% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Data from the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) showed that AI adoption among large enterprises in Singapore rose from 16.7% in 2018 to 44% in 2023.

sections.label: Company transformation and worker outcomes
sections.summary: Over 3,000 CTCs were formed, more than 480 transformation projects approved, and over 7,000 workers received wage increments, career development plans or skills allowances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Just to give an update, I am happy to update that we had formed over 3,000 CTCs to date, approved more than 480 transformation projects, helped over 7,000 workers receive an average of 5% wage increment above their annual increment or benefit from career development plans or from skills allowances.

sections.label: Precision engineering upskilling partnership
sections.summary: The first-of-its-kind programme seeks to upskill at least 1,000 workers and about 40 SMEs in ST Engineering Land Systems' Precision Engineering supplier network.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As a first of its kind partnership, the programme seeks to upskill at least 1,000 workers and about 40 SMEs within the Precision Engineering sector of the ST Engineering Land Systems’ supplier network while building on a robust ecosystem that offers both the breadth and the depth in technology and engineering capabilities.

sections.label: Union members training benefits
sections.summary: From 2022 to 2024, over 75,000 union members benefited from training through NCF and UTAP, reflecting 22% average annual growth in skills development.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: From 2022 to 2024, over 75,000 union members have benefited from training through NCF and UTAP, reflecting a 22% average annual growth in skills development.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance of up to $3,000 monthly for selected full-time courses, extended to part-time courses from early 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement is therefore grateful to hear that individuals can apply for the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance of up to $3,000 per month for selected full-time courses, and it will be extended to selected part-time courses from early 2026.

sections.label: NTUC career and job centres
sections.summary: NTUC expanded from two to 27 career and job centres, with around 110,000 jobseekers placed since February 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
