sentences.text: To support workers’ training and employment facilitation, NTUC has expanded in the national personalised placement landscape from two to 27 career and job centres, with around 110,000 jobseekers placed since February 2020.

sections.label: CTCs and training programme funding
sections.summary: NTUC helped establish over 3,000 CTCs and funded 480 training programmes, and the Government announced an additional $200 million for the CTC initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To date, NTUC has helped establish over 3,000 CTCs and funded 480 training programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This year, the Government announced an additional $200 million to support the CTC initiative.

sections.label: Budget 2025 and surpluses
sections.summary: Budget 2025 deepens areas from last year's Budget, which ended fiscal year 2024 with an estimated $6.4 billion surplus, and is forecast to end with a $6.8 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2025 continues the path forward, deepening and strengthening many areas covered from last year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is commendable that we managed to achieve much through last year's Budget and still end the fiscal year 2024 with an estimated surplus of $6.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, Budget 2025, with extensive immediate support initiatives and significant longer-term investment for our future, is forecast to end with another surplus of $6.8 billion.

sections.label: Suicide deaths in 2023
sections.summary: In 2023, 322 lives were lost to suicide based on Samaritans of Singapore statistics, the leading cause of death for those aged 10 to 29.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2023, based on statistics from the Samaritans of Singapore, we lost 322 lives to suicide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is the leading cause of death for those aged between 10 and 29.

sections.label: Youth suicide and self-harm data
sections.summary: Suicide remains the leading cause of death for nearly 30% of young people aged 10 to 29 over five consecutive years, and only 48.4% of studied patients had ongoing psychiatric or psychological support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to data from SOS, as mentioned earlier, suicide remains the leading cause of death for nearly 30% of young people aged between 10 and 29 over the last five consecutive years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on a study of 221 patients aged between 10 and 19 who were presented to hospitals’ emergency departments for suicidal or self-harm attempts in 2021, not all adolescents at risk of self-harm and suicidal behaviours have serious mental health disorders but, instead, have psychosocial problems and emotional regulation difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of these, only 48.4% of the patients studied had ongoing psychiatric or psychological support.

sections.label: Vulnerable groups suicide prevention recommendations
sections.summary: White Paper recommendations include strengthening governance and involving at-risk communities and people with lived experience in suicide prevention policymaking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Recommendations for vulnerable groups in the White Paper include strengthening governance and policy, involving communities of people at risk of suicide and those with lived experience of suicide in all aspects of policymaking and implementation of suicide prevention policies.

sections.label: School suicide prevention protocols and training
sections.summary: Passage calls for school suicide prevention protocols and training, citing concerns that educators lack skills to support at-risk students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Support schools and educators and, here, more specifically, to adolescents: establish suicide prevention protocols in schools for suicide prevention, crisis response and postvention support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In focus group discussions conducted under Project Hayat, participants have expressed concern that school staff, counsellors and teachers may be insufficiently equipped to provide psychological support or conduct suicide risk assessments for students in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It was also found that many educators may lack the necessary training to identify warning signs, manage crises or intervene effectively in suicide-related situations, leaving a critical gap in the support network for vulnerable students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By developing and implementing clear protocols and comprehensive training programmes, schools can ensure that educators, school counsellors and students are better prepared to respond to suicide risks.

sections.label: Funding challenges for smaller charities
sections.summary: Smaller charities face funding challenges and are essential to address gaps, with hopes that named groups channel resources to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: Many smaller charities will find funding a continuing challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: Smaller charities will be essential to address gaps as we work towards the objective of caring for everyone who needs help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: I hope the three groups mentioned by the Prime Minister, the Community Chest, the Collective for a Stronger Society and the President's Challenge will find ways to channel this increase in resources to some of the smaller charities who will be essential in ensuring that no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: The multiplier effect when everyone who can, gives, will be extraordinary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: I hope future Budgets will continue to nurture the spirit of giving and see greater collaboration between public and private initiatives that will ensure that no one is left behind.

sections.label: Increase in WIS payments
sections.summary: WIS payments will increase to $1.4 billion this year, benefitting half a million lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I appreciate the Government's commitment to continuously enhance WIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This year, WIS payments will increase to $1.4 billion, benefitting half a million lower-wage workers.

sections.label: WIS age cap at 60
sections.summary: WIS payments increase with age but currently max out at 60 years old, though many workers continue working beyond that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: WIS payments increases with age, but currently max out at 60 years old, even though many workers continue working well beyond that.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary wage floor
sections.summary: LQS serves as a wage floor, with the threshold raised from $1,400 to $1,600 and $10.50 per hour for part-time employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It serves as an important wage floor, ensuring that lower-wage workers receive a minimum level of pay across various sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We appreciate the Government's efforts in increasing the LQS to keep pace with rising local wages, such as the recent increase from $1,400 to $1,600 announced in Budget 2024, with the LQS threshold for part-time local employees raised to $10.50 per hour.

sections.label: WorkCare Grant applications closed
sections.summary: The WorkCare Grant, introduced by MOM in 2021 for rest areas for outsourced staff, closed to applications on 31 August 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2021, I raised this issue in the House and, in the same year, the WorkCare Grant was introduced by MOM to provide financial support for companies setting up rest areas for outsourced staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: However, applications for the Grant have closed since 31 August 2023.

sections.label: Leave resetting for outsourced workers
sections.summary: MOM statistics show 18,800 first-year resident employees get seven days' leave, and outsourced workers' leave may reset when contractors change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The MOM statistics show that 18,800 full-time resident employees in their first year of employment are receiving only seven days of paid annual leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For outsourced workers, each time a service buyer changes contractors, their leave entitlements may be reset, even if they continue in the same job, at the same site.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Although tripartite advisories encourage continuity of benefits, they appear insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to work with NTUC and our unions to conduct a thorough review of leave resetting for outsourced workers and explore stronger measures to protect them from unfair disadvantages.

sections.label: Support for FA4 success
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to keep strengthening support for skills upgrading, job placement and career transition programmes for FA4's success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As part of our efforts to ensure the success of FA4, I call on the Government to continue strengthening support for skills upgrading, job placement initiatives and career transition programmes.

sections.label: Unemployed PMETs in 2024 report
sections.summary: The Labour Force 2024 Report showed about 41,200 unemployed PMET residents, of whom 10,700 were unemployed over six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Labour Force 2024 Report showed that some 41,200 PMET residents are unemployed and, of these, 10,700 have been unemployed for more than six months.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level Up and Jobseeker Support
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Level Up gives those 40 and above $4,000 credit and training allowances, while SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support offers up to $6,000 over six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Level Up programme provides Singaporeans aged 40 and above with $4,000 in SkillsFuture credit, along with a training allowance of 50% of their average income over the latest available 12-month period, capped at $3,000 a month for selected full-time courses and $300 a month for selected part-time courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Skills Future Jobseeker Support scheme, which bears similarities with the Unemployment Insurance schemes proposed by the Workers' Party since 2006, will also offer financial support of up to $6,000 over six months for involuntarily unemployed workers taking part in job search or related activities.

sections.label: CCP training hiring barrier
sections.summary: The CCP requires employers to hire workers before training, creating the same barriers for jobseekers already struggling with initial screening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The CCP requires employers to hire the workers before they can receive training, presenting the same barriers for jobseekers who are already struggling to get past the initial job screening process.

sections.label: WSG returnship programmes proposal
sections.summary: WSG can introduce structured returnship programmes to help professionals re-enter the workforce after a career break, providing employment and mentorship without starting at entry level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Additionally, WSG can introduce structured returnship programmes to help professionals re-enter the workforce after a career break, whether due to retrenchment or caregiving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unlike the CCP, which requires career conversion, these returnship programmes would provide a pathway to employment and mentorship, allowing mid-career professionals to rebuild industry-relevant experience without starting over at entry level positions.

sections.label: Overlooking workers' experience and skills
sections.summary: The nation and economy cannot afford to overlook the experience and skills of these workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our nation and our economy cannot afford to overlook the experience and skills of these workers.

sections.label: Slower 2025 growth forecast
sections.summary: Slower growth of between 1% and 3% is expected in 2025, reflecting global headwinds and trade uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Slower growth is expected in 2025 of between 1% and 3%, reflecting global headwinds and trade uncertainties.

sections.label: FY2024 and Budget 2025 surpluses
sections.summary: Singapore reported a FY2024 Budget surplus of $6.4 billion, while Budget 2025 expects a $6.8 billion surplus driven by corporate income tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In FY2024, Singapore reported a Budget surplus of $6.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This was primarily attributed to an unexpected surge in corporate income tax collections, while Budget 2025 expects a surplus of $6.8 billion, driven by higher expected operating revenues, with corporate income tax as the greatest driver at $32.7 billion, or an increase of 5.8% from FY2024.

sections.label: NIRC projection rise
sections.summary: The Net Investment Returns Contribution is projected to rise from $24 billion in 2024 to $27.1 billion in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On the topic of projections, the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) is projected to rise from $24 billion in 2024 to $27.1 billion in 2025, an increase that is higher than the prior year.

sections.label: Carbon tax increase business costs
sections.summary: Singapore's carbon tax is slated to increase from $25 currently to up to S$80 by 2030, which will increase business costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With Singapore’s carbon tax slated to increase from $25 currently, to up to S$80 by 2030, this will also increase business costs.

sections.label: Equity Market Development Programme
sections.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced a $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme, which the passage calls a welcomed move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The recent Monetary Authority of Singapore announcement of the $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme is a welcomed move.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses
sections.summary: Scam cases rose over 10% to nearly 50,000 in 2024, with losses up 70% to more than $1.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Scam cases rose by over 10% to nearly 50,000 in 2024, while losses surged by 70% to more than $1.1 billion, despite stronger enforcement and technological safeguards.

sections.label: New young drug abusers
sections.summary: In 2024, 126 new drug abusers under age 20 were arrested, 30% more than 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2024, there were 126 new drug abusers under the age of 20 arrested, which is 30% more than 2023.

sections.label: Budget support for workers
sections.summary: The Budget places workers' interests at its core, emphasising households and families, and cites Youth Panels, the ITE Progression Award and Workfare Skills Support enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This year's Budget is one that truly uplifts all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It particularly places workers' interests at its core, with particular emphasis on supporting households and families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have seen the Youth Panels supported by the National Youth Council give our young people a voice in national discourse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have witnessed the ITE Progression Award providing graduates under 30 with both career opportunities and financial stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: And we have made significant strides towards becoming a more equitable society, with enhancements to the Workfare Skills Support Scheme enabling lower-wage workers to advance their skills earlier.

sections.label: Retrenchment and worker burnout
sections.summary: 2024 quarterly reports showed retrenchment incidence highest for residents aged 50 to 59 and rising for those 30 to 39, while a Telus Health survey found two-thirds of workers showed burnout signs.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Quarterly labour market reports for the first to third quarters of 2024 showed that while retrenchment incidence remained the highest for resident workers aged between 50 and 59, retrenchment incidence had risen for those aged between 30 and 39.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2024 survey by health technology provider Telus Health revealed that two-thirds of Singaporean workers showed signs of burnout, particularly those under the age of 40.

sections.label: Vulnerability of agency workers
sections.summary: The passage states agency workers are more likely to be on statutory basic terms and conditions, and may become vulnerable to decaying skills and shortchanged compensation if regulations are not upheld.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: You just ring up the agency and say, 'We don't want them coming back in.' If you have an agency workforce, they're more likely to be on the statutory basic terms and conditions – minimum holiday, minimum wage, minimum rest breaks." If user firms and staffing agencies fail to respect and uphold employment regulations and fair employment practices, agency workers will become increasingly vulnerable to decaying skills and being shortchanged in compensation, particularly those who are lower-wage and lower-skilled.

sections.label: Falling Singapore fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate fell from 1.12 in 2021 to 0.97 in 2023, after leading in only three global industries by 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2021, they only led in three global industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Turning to Singapore, Singapore's TFR has been falling, from 1.12 in 2021 to 0.97 in 2023.

sections.label: Budget 2025 and stock market
sections.summary: Budget 2025, with a $5 billion programme to strengthen the Singapore stock market, will fuel a dynamic and evolving Singapore economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Together with the $5 billion programme to strengthen the Singapore stock market, Budget 2025 will fuel a dynamic and evolving Singapore economy.

sections.label: Training support for agency workers
sections.summary: Without support and paid time-off for training, agency workers could face skills decay, so the $200 million CTC Grant allocation is appreciated.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Without support and paid time-off to attend training, agency workers could suffer from skills decay and these workers could become less and less valued by the market.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I appreciate the Government's allocation of the additional $200 million to NTUC's Company Training Committee Grant (CTC Grant) to help more companies transform and upskill their workers.

sections.label: CTC approach for sector agencies
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government would adopt the CTC approach for grant programmes managed by sector agencies, working with unions.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Work with unions to power a flywheel of momentum that strengthens the people who will build your business with you.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, would the Government consider adopting the CTC approach for grant programmes managed by sector agencies?

sections.label: Protection for freelancers and agency workers
sections.summary: Citing the Platform Workers Act, the passage asks whether the Government would strengthen legal protection of freelancers and agency workers, including creative freelancers' rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We could take a leaf from the Government’s approach to platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Then, the whole-of-Government leaned forward for platform workers and rolled out the new Platform Workers Act this year with strong support from platform operators and NTUC’s platform work associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Platform workers can now be represented, protected and supported.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, would the Government consider strengthening legal protection of freelancers and agency workers?

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Creative freelancers look to the Government to instil in service buyers, respect for creatives’ intellectual property rights and rights to timely payment and fair terms, and to uphold justice if buyers wilfully violate such rights.

sections.label: SkillsFuture training for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government would increase accessible SkillsFuture training courses and guide providers to accommodate persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To further uplift persons with disabilities, would the Government consider increasing the range of accessible SkillsFuture training courses, including guiding training providers to provide reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities to attend the training?

sections.label: Local PME fair treatment measures
sections.summary: The speaker says past advocacy for local PME measures was answered by COMPASS and the Workplace Fairness Act, which protects against age and nationality discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, I have advocated for a compendium of measures to level the playing field for our local PMEs, including stronger deterrence against errant employers who discriminate against Singaporeans, a foreign PME dependency ratio, stricter Employment Pass application conditions, continuous enhancements to the Fair Consideration Framework, and many others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am heartened that these calls have been answered through the implementation of the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) and the recent passing of the landmark Workplace Fairness Act, which protects workers against the most common types of workplace discrimination, such as age and nationality.

sections.label: Retrenchment and Singaporean priority
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to require employers to notify and compensate early and prioritise Singaporeans for jobs and career support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Where retrenchment is unavoidable, I strongly urge the Government to take a firmer stance in ensuring that employers not just give early notification to unions and affected workers and compensate them fairly but also prioritise Singaporeans for job opportunities and career support.

sections.label: Skills training and leadership schemes
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes SkillsFuture grants, a $200 million NTUC CTC Grant top-up, and resources to groom Singaporean workers as corporate leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This means investing in skills training and creating more opportunities for career progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant, the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, and the $200 million top-up of NTUC’s CTC Grant to help companies offset workforce transformation costs and support job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: After years of lobbying, I am also glad that more resources will be set aside for schemes that groom Singaporean workers to become leaders in the corporate sector by sending them for overseas work postings and leadership milestone programmes.

sections.label: Workers' job loss concerns
sections.summary: NTUC's latest Survey on Economic Sentiments found 34% of workers, including PMEs, worried about losing jobs or contract renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In NTUC's latest Survey on Economic Sentiments, 34% of workers, including PMEs, expressed concerns about losing their jobs or not having their contracts renewed in the next couple of months.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up mid-career support
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the SkillsFuture Level-Up programme's $4,000 credit top-up and monthly allowances, citing a World Economic Forum reskilling projection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Despite this, they remained positive about upskilling as an enabler to take up higher-value work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am therefore happy that the Government has heeded our calls for greater support for mid-career workers through the SkillsFuture Level-Up programme, which offers a $4,000 credit top-up and monthly allowances for those who take time off to pursue full-time training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: According to the World Economic Forum, 70% of Singapore's workforce will need to undergo reskilling or upskilling by 2030.

sections.label: Basic HR certification requirement
sections.summary: A Joint NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce recommendation is to improve HR standards; the speaker urges tripartite work on basic HR certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: One key recommendation that emerged from the Joint NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce is to enhance fair employment practices through improving HR standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to work with tripartite partners to develop requirements for basic HR certification, either by IHRP or other internationally recognised organisations of equivalence.

sections.label: Strengthening 3Cs for workers
sections.summary: Singapore must strengthen Core, Compact and Capability, as investing in and protecting workers throughout life has made the nation prosper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To ride the wave of change, be ahead of the curve, and not be hit by curveballs, we need to strengthen the 3Cs – Core, Compact and Capability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the past 60 years, Singapore has stood in solidarity with our workers during times of crisis and change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: From industrialising in our early days, to the Financial Crisis in 2008, to the more recent COVID-19 pandemic, we knew that the only way to move forward is to do so as One United People.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Yet, one truth remains constant – when we invest in and protect and equip our workers throughout life, our entire nation prospers.

sections.label: Budget surplus and SG60 vouchers
sections.summary: This Budget follows $6-plus billion surpluses for FY2024 and FY2025, setting aside about $3 billion for CDC and SG60 vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It has become quintessentially Singaporean, it permeates all our Budgets, but it is special and, indeed, it is exceptional.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This Budget comes on the back of a $6-plus billion surplus for FY2024 and another $6-plus billion in surplus projected for FY2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Instead, the Government has set aside just about $3 billion in this Budget on CDC and SG60 vouchers and just about 5% of the Budget on cost-of-living support measures and the SG60 package overall and left that $13 billion surplus over these two FYs on the table, in an election year.

sections.label: Rethink senior means-testing framework
sections.summary: The means-testing framework based primarily on per capita income for allocating support to seniors is due for a fundamental rethink.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, on this note, I wish to make three suggestions – not about deploying more resources, but about achieving a more effective allocation of the resources that we are deploying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I put it to this House that our framework to determine which senior gets how much support – in other words, our means-testing framework, based primarily on per capita income (PCI), to determine how resources to support seniors are allocated, is due for a fundamental rethink, in order to remain fit for purpose in our super-aged future.

sections.label: Per capita income and senior support
sections.summary: Under per capita income means-testing, an elderly couple whose adult child moves out is treated as a zero-income household, affecting CHAS, Silver Support and hospital subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But if, instead, this single, adult child moves out and stays separately from his or her parents, then in one stroke, the elderly couple is now taken as one household, on their own, with zero income and deemed in our current means-testing framework to have much less means, even if it can be said that a single child who is able to buy and move out to his or her own place probably has more means to support his or her parents, compared with someone who does not have his or her own place and continues to stay with his or her parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This current means-testing framework, based on per capita income, can mean all the difference for our seniors; whether they qualify for a Blue or Green CHAS card; whether they get Silver Support every three months or not; whether they get 80% or 60% or lower subsidies in a B2/C-class ward in our public hospitals and so on.

sections.label: Decouple senior means-testing framework
sections.summary: The suggestion is to decouple the means-testing framework for seniors from that for working-age adults and young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: My suggestion is to decouple the means-testing framework for seniors from the means-testing framework for the rest of the population – for working-age adults and young children – going forward.

sections.label: Use lifetime CPF contributions
sections.summary: Move away from household per capita income towards a senior's lifetime earnings, proxied by lifetime CPF contributions at the individual level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Move away from per capita income at the household level, towards a senior's lifetime earnings primarily, proxied by lifetime contributions to his or her CPF, at the individual level.

sections.label: ITE and polytechnic per-student spending
sections.summary: Government recurrent spending is around $16,000 per ITE student versus around $18,000 per full-time diploma student, a $2,000 gap consistent since at least 2012-2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, we are spending around $16,000 per student in ITE, compared to around $18,000 per full-time diploma programme student, primarily in polytechnics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, Government recurrent spending on ITE is around $2,000 lower per student compared to its spending on polytechnics; and this difference of $2,000 per student has been quite consistent since at least 2012, 2013.

sections.label: Educating educators and adult educators
sections.summary: It states that educator training is focused through NIEC and NIE, and proposes a sharpened mandate for the Institute for Adult Learning and uplifting adult educators' stature and pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In both the pre-school and formal schooling systems, we have established and maintained a laser-sharp focus on educating the educators, through the National Institute of Early Childhood Development and National Institute of Education respectively, to ensure a high quality of educators in these spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Establish a laser-sharp focus on educating the adult educators through a sharpened mandate for the Institute for Adult Learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Two, let us uplift the stature, recognition and career advancement pathways for our adult educators and trainers in Singapore.

sections.label: Adult education teaching and scholarships
sections.summary: It states the best faculty must also teach adult education, and proposes creating scholarships for the adult education and training space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In our autonomous universities and our polytechnics and our ITE Colleges, the best educators and faculty members must not go to undergraduate teaching only; the best must also teach in adult education and training, and be part of that fraternity of adult education practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Three, let us create scholarships for the adult education and training space, just as we have done for both the preschool and formal schooling systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Let us create scholarships, to attract and capture a fair share of our best talents, to become both adult educators, and educators of these adult educators.

sections.label: Conversations on Singapore Women's Development
sections.summary: In 2020, NTUC partnered with SCWO and PA WIN to lead the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development, engaging nearly 6,000 participants in over 160 sessions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2020, NTUC partnered with the Singapore Council of Women’s Organisations and the People's Association Women Integration Network to lead the Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These dialogues engaged nearly 6,000 participants, across more than 160 conversation sessions.

sections.label: Flexible work and workplace fairness efforts
sections.summary: It cites the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests and the Workplace Fairness Legislation as examples of these efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Examples of these efforts include the introduction of the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests (TG-FWAR) and the Workplace Fairness Legislation.

sections.label: Programme expansion, mentors and mentees
sections.summary: Since its launch, the programme has expanded to 10 constituencies, with 300 mentors and 300 mentees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Since its launch, the programme has steadily expanded, now reaching 10 constituencies across the island, with 300 mentors and 300 mentees.

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood Survey
sections.summary: A Marriage and Parenthood Survey by the NTUC Women and Family Unit and PAP Women's Wing with over 1,000 respondents revealed key Government priorities for parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A recently concluded Marriage and Parenthood Survey, conducted by the NTUC Women and Family Unit and PAP Women’s Wing with over 1,000 respondents, revealed key Government priorities for our parents.

sections.label: CUB Programme expansion
sections.summary: The CUB Programme will expand to PME jobs like accounting and office administration, and be re-engineered to cover new to the workforce pregnant mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The CUB Programme will now expand to PME jobs such as accounting and office administration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, the NTUC Woman and Family Unit will re-engineer our CUB Programme to cover new to the workforce pregnant mothers, ensuring that they enjoy their full maternity benefits while being secured of permanent employment after their delivery.

sections.label: Support for SMEs employing women
sections.summary: In light of Budget 2025 announcements, the Government is called on to consider additional support to SMEs employing a higher number of women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In light of Singapore's Budget 2025 announcements, which encourages Singaporean to have larger families, and given that women are child bearers and traditionally take on a larger share of caregiving, we call on the Government to consider additional support to SMEs that employ a higher number of women.

sections.label: Getting To-Gather: Power of Women
sections.summary: Clinics evolved into Getting To-Gather: Power of Women, building employer-migrant domestic worker relations, with families asking for temporary monthly work permits for replacement workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our clinics have since evolved into a programme, Getting To-Gather: Power of Women (POW).

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Under this programme, we brought in resources and partnerships to build healthy employer-migrant domestic workers relations, such as the Centre for Domestic Employees, Rice Company and the Association of Employment Agencies, amongst others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our POW events are well-attended with attendees in the 100s, and feature care carnivals and awards that celebrate the positive relationships between migrant domestic workers and their employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, our families have asked for further assistance on being able to get temporary monthly work permits for replacement migrant domestic workers when their permanent helper goes on home leave.

sections.label: Hawkers and merchants discounts
sections.summary: Led by three hawkers' and merchants' associations, participating hawkers, merchants and market stallholders contributed over $500,000 in discounts to residents in seven months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Led by our three hawkers' and merchants' associations, the participating hawkers, merchants and market stallholders have contributed more than $500,000 worth of discounts to our residents in the past seven months.

sections.label: FairPrice Group discounts and rebates
sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2024, NTUC FairPrice Group provided about $330 million in discounts and LinkPoints rebates to card holders to ease household financial burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, the NTUC FairPrice Group provided approximately $330 million in Pioneer Generation, Merdeka Generation, Senior Citizen and CHAS discount card holders, as well as LinkPoints rebates to help ease the financial burdens on households.

sections.label: CASE pre-payment loss statistics
sections.summary: CASE's annual complaints statistics show consumers lost close to $2 million in pre-payment losses in 2024, over four times 2023 losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the annual complaints statistics by the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE), consumers suffered close to $2 million in pre-payment losses in 2024, this is more than quadruple, four times of the losses reported in 2023.

sections.label: CASE president urges consumer law review
sections.summary: The CASE president urges the Government to convene a panel to comprehensively review and update consumer protection laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: As president of CASE, I urge the Government to convene a panel to comprehensively review and update our consumer protection laws.

sections.label: Unit pricing on Price Kaki app
sections.summary: CASE's Price Kaki app has unit pricing for over 6,000 items since 2023, and the president urges mandating unit pricing in all major retail stores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Locally, the Price Kaki app launched by CASE has already implemented unit pricing in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We now have unit pricing on the app for over 6,000 items, including groceries and household products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since its implementation, we have received much positive feedback on the usefulness of the unit pricing feature; and I am of the view that the time is now right for unit pricing to go beyond the Price Kaki app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to mandate the display of unit pricing in all major online and physical retail stores.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model expansion and wages
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model has expanded to nine sectors covering over 155,000 lower-wage workers, with cumulative wage increases of 11% from 2017 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: With the strong support of our tripartite partners, what started with the cleaning sector has now expanded into nine sectors and occupations, covering more than 155,000 lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: From 2017 to 2022, PWM workers in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors saw a cumulative wage increase of 11%.

sections.label: Older worker employment and training rates
sections.summary: Employment, wages and training participation for older workers aged 50 and above have risen between 2014 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The employment rate of older workers aged 55 to 64 has risen from 66.3% in 2014 to 70.4% in last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Wages for workers aged 50 and above have also risen faster than median income.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age increase

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Government has also supported the tripartite consensus and announced the next statutory increase in the retirement and re-employment ages to 64 and 69 respectively, to take place from 1 July 2026.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment
sections.summary: The Government is convening a Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment to take stock of headwinds and forge consensus for businesses and older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In this regard, it is opportune that the Government is convening a Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment to frankly and cohesively take stock of these ongoing headwinds and forge new consensus and effective ways of maximising value for both businesses and our older workers.

sections.label: NTUC survey on older workers
sections.summary: NTUC's Survey on Economic Sentiments 2025 found career confidence decreases with age, with 43% of workers 55 and above reporting it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The NTUC's Survey on Economic Sentiments 2025 found that workers' career confidence decreases as they get older.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: When older workers, those 55 years old and above, are asked, 43% had that confidence.

sections.label: Thanking Government for CTC funding
sections.summary: The speaker joins fellow Labour Members of Parliament in thanking the Government for a $250 million further injection supporting the CTCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Here, I join my fellow Labour Members of Parliament in thanking the Government for the $250 million further injection in support of the CTCs.

sections.label: Integrating manpower, social, health solutions
sections.summary: The speaker says it is time to relook at integrating manpower, social and health solutions as a continuum to enable middle-aged caregivers to return to work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And that, pairing up with the availability of flexible work arrangements on the company's side, that will make things happen.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I believe that, since then, and with the more recent advent of initiatives, such as the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) Healthier SG, Age Well SG and various relevant initiatives on the part of MOM, I think this is a time for us to really relook how we can look at integrating the solutions both on the manpower or the labour market side as well as on the social and health side as a continuum in order to enable this return to work to happen for middle-aged caregivers in a substantial way.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As a result, we have made very substantial progress for our older workers, often bucking global trends.

sections.label: Seniors' share of suicide cases
sections.summary: Seniors aged 60 and above now account for nearly 30% of suicide cases in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Seniors aged 60 and above now account for nearly 30% of suicide cases in Singapore.

sections.label: Pre-retirement planning and mental health
sections.summary: The speaker calls on MOH and MOM to collaborate on pre-retirement planning and consider incentivising structured mental health programmes for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The loss of these can lead to anxiety, depression and even cognitive decline, if not addressed early.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I call on MOH and MOM to collaborate with employers and unions to incorporate pre-retirement planning that prepares young seniors in their 60s emotionally for this transition.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Government can consider incentivising companies, unions and associations like the Singapore National Employers' Federation to implement structured mental health programmes for seniors, similar to the support we provide businesses hiring seniors.

sections.label: Social connection for seniors
sections.summary: Social connection is described as the most powerful safeguard against mental health decline in seniors.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Social connection is the most powerful safeguard against mental health decline in seniors.

sections.label: Peer-led support reduces isolation
sections.summary: Silver Ribbon and Samaritans of Singapore show peer-led support from those with similar challenges effectively reduces senior isolation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Organisations like Silver Ribbon and the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) have shown that peer-led support, particularly from those who have navigated similar challenges, is highly effective in reducing isolation amongst our seniors.

sections.label: Grants for retired seniors
sections.summary: The passage proposes extending grants, similar to youth-led initiative grants, to retired seniors starting community programmes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: To further empower them, I propose extending grants, similar to those given to youths-led initiatives, to retired seniors interested in starting community programmes.

sections.label: English mental health resources
sections.summary: Most mental health resources in Singapore are in English, leaving non-English-speaking seniors underserved.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Most mental health resources in Singapore are in English, leaving non-English-speaking seniors underserved.

sections.label: Paracounsellors, religious leaders, scam reporting
sections.summary: It proposes training paracounsellors, government collaboration with religious organisations, and empowering Community Centre Teams as scam reporting points.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Training paracounsellors within these communities can provide support, and when religious leaders share their personal stories about mental health challenges, it not only humanises the issue but also encourages the congregants to seek help without fear of judgement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I encourage the Government to collaborate more closely with religious organisations in reaching out to our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: To address this, I propose empowering the Community Centre Teams as points of contact for seniors to report scams, offering a more approachable alternative to contacting the Police.

sections.label: Caregiver savings and support services
sections.summary: It proposes caregiver savings schemes, financial assistance, expanded training and respite services, including for foreign domestic workers in dementia care.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Many caregivers, particularly those who are the sole, unmarried children of the seniors, sacrifice their career and personal savings, often leading to financial insecurity in their own later years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I propose the Government to consider solutions like dedicated caregiver savings schemes, leveraging CPF contributions and providing financial assistance to families in need, as I raised in Parliament in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Additionally, we must expand training and respite services for caregivers, ensuring affordable, accessible programmes and support.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: These services should also extend to foreign domestic workers, who play a critical role in dementia care and face high stress and burnout.

sections.label: Mental well-being and disconnecting
sections.summary: The passage states that calls about mental well-being for seniors and the right to disconnect are quite loud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Whether it is about mental well-being for seniors or the right to disconnect, I think the call is quite loud.

sections.label: Culture Pass for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Culture Pass is now issued broadly to every Singaporean aged 18 and above, signalling that the arts are essential.

sentences.text: With the Culture Pass now being issued broadly to every Singaporean aged 18 and above, the Government has sent a clear signal: the arts are essential to our society, just like any other basic necessity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, will the Culture Pass be transferable, or can unused credits be donated to arts charities, in the same way that can be done for CDC Vouchers?

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The concern here is that arts groups could inflate ticket prices, knowing that a subsidy is now available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I see from guidelines that were issued this week that the scheme will eventually include the purchase of local books.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This was a 40-fold increase in price from its last auction in 1998.

sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2023 Singapore's share of global art trade by value grew from 1% to 5%, with 42% new collectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the report, between 2019 and 2023, Singapore had expanded its share by value of artworks from 1% to 5% of the global trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore also had the highest proportion of new collectors, at 42% and spent the most on new and emerging artists' works in 2023 and the first half of 2024.

sections.label: Art investment fund comparison
sections.summary: An art investment fund could attract capital like MAS' $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme does.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme seeks to attract capital from institutional investors, family offices and private entities, an art investment fund could potentially do the same.

sections.label: Global Investor Programme arts inclusion
sections.summary: GIP requires foreign investors to make qualifying investments for PR, already includes arts businesses, and will be refined this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Global Investor Programme (GIP), for example, requires foreign investors to deploy a portion of their wealth into qualifying investments in order to be eligible for Singapore Permanent Residency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: GIP will be refined this year with the specific aim of strengthening the competitiveness of Singapore's equities market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The scheme actually already includes arts businesses within its scope of qualifying industries, which is an important inclusion, but more can be done to connect arts businesses, especially promising startups, with these potential investors.

sections.label: Tuition industry and education budget
sections.summary: The tuition industry receives $1.8 billion a year from parents, alongside a $14.75 billion Ministry of Education budget last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us take stock on what we have now: a tuition industry that is fueled by $1.8 billion a year from anxious parents, combined with a budget of $14.75 billion last year from the Ministry of Education.

sections.label: Youth mental health and fertility
sections.summary: Nearly a third of young people aged 15 to 35 reported symptoms like feeling empty, tense or upset, and total fertility rate is at an all-time low.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nearly a third of our young people aged 15 to 35 reported symptoms that included feeling empty, tense or upset most of the time, according to the National Youth Mental Health Study.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our total fertility rate is at an all-time low.

sections.label: Education assessment model revamp
sections.summary: The proposal suggests removing high-stakes exams, letting students choose assessment topics, expanding free time, and revamping PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To build on the progress made, I propose a further revamp of our education assessment models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, we can remove high-stakes examinations in favour of continuous, diverse assessments that factor in classroom participation, socioemotional skills, creativity and interpersonal skills, and we can start these in primary school; two, allow students to choose topics of interest for assessments, such as selecting preferred oral exam topics rather than answering pre-set questions; three, expand structured free time within school hours for students to engage in non-structured exploration, such as outdoor, community and cultural excursions without fear of falling behind their peers; and four, revamp the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) to lower a paper-based weightage in favour of alternative assessment methods, such as performance tasks, presentations and portfolio-building, based on real-world applications and personal interest.

sections.label: Low fertility rate incentives
sections.summary: The speaker says financial incentives alone are insufficient to address Singapore's low fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I will now address our low fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, the hard truth is this: financial incentives alone are insufficient.

sections.label: Psychological barriers to parenthood
sections.summary: Psychological barriers such as career fears, work-life balance and hypercompetitiveness dissuade young couples from parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The psychological barriers, such as fear of lost career progression, concerns over work-life balance and the daunting prospect of raising children in a hypercompetitive society, continue to dissuade young couples from embracing parenthood, and I say it is understandably so.

sections.label: Depressurising the education system
sections.summary: Depressurising education would let couples spend on family pursuits instead of tuition and enrichment classes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As an imperative, depressurising the education system would allow young couples to feel better able to channel their finances to lifestyle and aspirational pursuits as a family rather than having to spend hefty sums on tuition and enrichment classes, which really makes for a very poor parent-child relationship.

sections.label: Building a family-friendly society
sections.summary: The nation must build support systems and reshape narratives around family, success metrics and parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our nation must acknowledge that fostering a more family-friendly society is not merely about easing financial burdens but also about building within society, the support systems that enable parenting to be less stressful, more joyful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to take the lead in dialling down on pragmatism and amping up on the feel-good "cuddle" factor in our conversations around parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is time to redefine our success metrics – from grades and rankings to personal fulfilment and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is time to reshape the narrative around family – from cost and sacrifice to joy and aspiration, to build a Singapore where both dreams and families can flourish.

sections.label: Europe and unbalanced multi-polarity
sections.summary: Europe re-evaluates its security posture amid trade shifts, an AI arms race and economic nationalism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And finally, a Europe facing a reckoning, forced to re-evaluate its security posture and reliance on the US and Russia and its future role on the global stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And this unbalanced multi-polarity is now playing out in new economic battlegrounds: one, tectonic shifts in global trade, trade fragmentation and regionalisation, slowing China-West trade while China-rest-of-world trade and South-South trade grows; two, a technology and artificial intelligence (AI) arms race, the semi-conductor wars, the AI diffusion rule, the arrival of DeepSeek; and three, economic nationalism, rising subsidies, tariff wars and trade barriers, a shift away from the World Trade Organization-led global trade governance.

sections.label: Economic performance after COVID-19
sections.summary: Four years after COVID-19, the economy grew 4.4%, real incomes rose 3.4% and income inequality is lowest since 2000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Four years after COVID-19, our economy grew 4.4%, real incomes are up 3.4%, corporate profits are up, inflation under control, income inequality lowest since records began in 2000.

sections.label: US tariffs impact
sections.summary: US tariffs on China, Mexico and Canada are estimated to raise tariff costs by US$250 billion, with steel and aluminium tariffs affecting all countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The impact of the 1 February 2025 US tariffs on China, Mexico and Canada is estimated to increase tariff costs by a whopping US$250 billion, materially impacting company profits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The 10 February 2025 steel and aluminium tariffs suggest that all countries will be affected in time, with impact dependent on trade balances and country concentration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Industrial goods, energy, electronics and data centres are the sectors expected to be most exposed.

sections.label: Nuclear power and SMRs
sections.summary: Nuclear power via small modular reactors is noteworthy, with the UK Rolls Royce programme forecast to create 40,000 jobs and £52 billion by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This not only has implications for our net-zero goals, but also limits economic development in growth sectors, like AI, advanced manufacturing, semi-conductors and biopharmaceutical.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Thus, the potential deployment of nuclear power in the form of small modular reactors (SMRs) is noteworthy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One of the first SMR programmes in the world, the Rolls Royce SMR programme in the UK, when fully operational, is forecast to create 40,000 regional jobs in the UK by 2050 and generate £52 billion in economic benefit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The $5 billion top-up to the Future Energy Fund to invest in nuclear electricity imports and hydrogen is timely.

sections.label: Budget 2025 support extension

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Budget 2025 continues that evolution, extending support to those over 30 and training allowances to part-time programmes.

sections.label: Woodlands Youth Adulting Programme
sections.summary: A Youth Adulting Programme in Woodlands will help young adults learn about careers, skills, entrepreneurship, technology, innovation, financial literacy, mental health and relationships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Woodlands, we are launching a Youth Adulting Programme that will help young adults learn about careers, skills, entrepreneurship, technology and innovation, along with financial literacy, mental health and building relationships, which I jokingly tell my team it starts with a healthy date.

sections.label: Large Family Scheme childcare fees

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Large Family Scheme and lower childcare fee caps will help many families in Woodlands.

sections.label: Woodlands community assistance programmes

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Belanja-a-Meal@Woodlands, which has been running for five years, giving hawker meals to 300 beneficiaries, and Store@Woodlands, which has been running for four years, giving 400-plus families groceries of their choice, are funded almost entirely by sponsors, schools, preschools, residents and the general public, not by Government funds, because they believe in our cause.

sections.label: Singapore neutrality and global role
sections.summary: Singapore must maintain neutrality, act in its national interest, and can bridge China and the West amid global disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will we be forced to pick a side?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have maintained our neutrality, acting in our national interest, and we must continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Despite our size, Singapore is respected for pragmatic, principles-based strategic diplomacy, balancing relations between the US, China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, Singapore now has a duty to step up, to be a bridge between China and the West, to reduce tensions and improve global cooperation and integration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need Singaporean officials on global forums, and we need Singaporean talents to step up into leadership roles in companies that operate in the geopolitical arena, as their understanding of China and the US, uniquely positions them to add value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: The years ahead could be stormy, where extreme weather patterns, disease outbreaks, protracted conflicts and great power competition converge to induce global disruptions of increased frequency and magnitude.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: We must view every disruption as an opportunity – an opportunity to strengthen our supply chains, to protect our planet, to empower our people and to increase our international influence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Together, as one united people, let us commit to building a resilient future, a resilient Singapore.

sections.label: National Productivity Fund top-up

sentences.text: So, we have to be prepared for tougher competition and do what we can to stay in the game.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are topping up the National Productivity Fund, which will provide us extra firepower to stay competitive and attract investments.

sentences.text: Over the past decade, real wage growth has been commensurate with productivity growth.
