sections.summary: In the Budget Statement, a comprehensive study on post-18 pathways for people with disabilities was announced.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In my Budget Statement, I said we are embarking on a comprehensive study to look at post-18 pathways for people with disabilities.

sections.label: Caregiving grant and care subsidies
sections.summary: The Budget enhanced the Home Caregiving Grant and increased subsidies for nursing home and community care services.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, we have significantly enhanced the Home Caregiving Grant and increased subsidies for care services in nursing homes and in the community.

sections.label: Social spending exceeds economy and security
sections.summary: Social spending is greater than spending on the economy and security combined.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, we spend more on social development than on the economy and security.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Actually, social spending is already greater than what we spend on both the economy and security combined.

sections.label: More matching grants for fundraising
sections.summary: The Budget provides more matching grants for fundraising efforts, which Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Keith Chua welcomed.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, we are supporting them further with more matching grants for their fundraising efforts, something which Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Keith Chua welcomed.

sections.label: Liquidated money laundering assets to Consolidated Fund
sections.summary: Assets from the $3 billion money laundering case surrendered to the state are being liquidated and added to the Consolidated Fund as overall revenues.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about the assets linked to the $3 billion money laundering case, which have been surrendered to the state.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These assets are progressively being liquidated and, when they are liquidated, monies will be added to the Consolidated Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These funds are not earmarked for specific purposes but will be part of our overall revenues to fund the Government's Budget.

sections.label: Corporate income tax upsides and FY2024 deficit
sections.summary: Without unexpected corporate income tax collection upsides from the last two years, FY2024 would have ended in a deficit.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Or if we did not enjoy the unexpected upsides in corporate income tax collections, which emerged only in the last two years?

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We would have ended FY2024 in a deficit.

sections.label: Deviation in FY2023 and FY2024
sections.summary: In FY2023 and FY2024 the deviation was larger but still around 7%, comparable to the UK and the Netherlands.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the latest two financial years, FY2023 and FY2024, the deviation has been larger, but still around 7%, which is comparable still to other jurisdictions like the UK and the Netherlands.

sections.label: 2024 GDP growth exceeded projections
sections.summary: MTI projected 1% to 3% growth in early 2024, but the year ended with 4.4% GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Remember, in early 2024, MTI started the year projecting that the economy would grow at 1% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We ended 2024 with gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 4.4%, well exceeding our expectations.

sections.label: Additional COE quota lowered prices
sections.summary: Government action injecting additional COE quota brought prices down 10% to 30% from October 2023 peaks.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The higher collections were a result of Government action by injecting additional COE quota.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This helped to bring prices down by 10% to 30% from the peaks in October 2023.

sections.label: Balanced Budget and Past Reserves
sections.summary: Spending will stay within means and the Budget balanced over the medium term, so Past Reserves drawn during COVID-19 cannot be put back.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Even as our spending goes up, we will continue to keep within our means and maintain a balanced Budget over the medium term.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why I do not see us being able to put back the amount we had drawn from Past Reserves during COVID-19, something which Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about.

sections.label: Reserves protect Singaporeans
sections.summary: Reserves and fiscal strength enable protection of Singaporeans and turning adversity into opportunity.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our reserves and our fiscal strength will enable us to protect Singaporeans when it matters and to turn adversity into opportunity, to turn our vulnerabilities into strength.

sections.label: Benefits versus taxes by quintile
sections.summary: The bottom quintile receives $4 in benefits per dollar of tax paid; only the top quintile receives less, 30 cents.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The bottom quintile of households receives $4 in benefits for every dollar of tax paid.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, it is only the top quintile of income earners who receive less in benefits, or 30 cents, for every dollar of tax paid.

sections.label: OECD commends Singapore fiscal system
sections.summary: A recent OECD report commended Singapore on its robust fiscal system.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A recent Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) report commended Singapore on our robust fiscal system.

sections.label: Budget for Singapore's next lap
sections.summary: This year's Budget, anchored on the Forward SG agenda, aims to chart Singapore's next lap and secure its long-term future.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It has served us well these last 60 years and it will continue to keep Singapore on the right track in the years ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are contending with tectonic shifts on multiple fronts: geopolitics and trade, technology and energy, demographics and culture.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have a strong fiscal footing built up over years of careful stewardship by our forefathers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have a clear plan for the road ahead, anchored on our Forward SG agenda.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are grounded in our shared values of solidarity and unity.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This year's Budget paves the way for us to chart Singapore's next lap, to navigate uncertainties with gumption and strength, to address immediate challenges decisively, and to secure our long-term future with confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is a Budget put together by Singaporeans, with Singaporeans, for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Core inflation and corporate tax revenue
sections.summary: Core inflation for 2024 was 2.5% to 3.5%, and OECD-estimated corporate tax revenue gains would materialise only from FY2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With regard to core inflation for 2024, it was 2.5% to 3.5%, and it estimated that the GST rate increase would contribute slightly less than 1% to core inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the matter of the third subject, which was covered by the Prime Minister in his round-up speech, if I can just bring back what was mentioned at last year's Budget – when the Prime Minister was then Finance Minister – brought up in his round-up speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He confirmed that OECD estimated that the investment hubs, Singapore, being one of them, would stand to see corporate tax revenue gain ranging from $5 billion to $11 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But that, on a more conservative estimate, this was $2 billion to $11 billion, and these increases would only materialise from FY2027.

sections.label: Occasional paper on medium-term outlook
sections.summary: The Finance Minister said the occasional paper on fiscal trends will be updated, and MOF was asked to confirm its release with BEPS projections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister said also in his last Budget reply speech and I quote, "the occasional paper that we published last year may not be so occasional after all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We will keep on updating it from time to time so that everyone will have a sense of how our fiscal trends are unfolding, not just on a year-to-year basis, but over five-year and 10-year horizons." Can I confirm that MOF will be releasing this occasional paper on the medium-term outlook with BEPS reflected in its projections shortly?

sections.label: Climate Voucher not cost of living support
sections.summary: The speaker reiterated that the Climate Voucher is not a cost of living support measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On Climate Voucher, I should just reiterate, I understand his explanation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I was just making the point that this is not a cost of living support measure, the Climate Voucher.

sections.label: GST impact on price levels
sections.summary: MAS statements cited state that the impact of GST on price levels is once-off and transitory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On "turbocharging" of inflation and the explanation that Mr Singh provided, I think he would have also, if he had read the reply he cited, read other MAS statements, which stated very clearly the impact of GST on price levels is once-off and it is transitory.

sections.label: Updates on BEPS corporate income tax
sections.summary: No immediate updates on corporate income tax revenues from BEPS can be provided, but further updates on the medium-term fiscal position are committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Will it be more tit-for-tat-type taxes or will there be some global cooperation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that is why we are unable to provide any immediate updates to our corporate income tax revenues from BEPS in the near term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But certainly, as the situation gets clearer, we remain committed to providing further updates on our medium-term fiscal position, including revenues from BEPS, if any, pluses or minuses, and we will continue to publish these figures.

sections.label: Forward SG spending estimates
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said $5 billion is expected as a first instalment and close to $40 billion by the end of this decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Second clarification is, last year, the Prime Minister, the then-Deputy Prime Minister mentioned about the $5 billion that is expected to be spent on the Forward SG policy moves as a first instalment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Then he also mentioned that close to $40 billion is expected to be spent on the Forward SG policy moves by the end of this decade.

sections.label: Forward SG expenditure amounts
sections.summary: Forward SG expenditure was $5 billion in last year's Budget and about $5 billion will probably be spent this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On Forward SG expenditures, in last year's Budget, we said it was $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This year, we will probably spend about $5 billion as well.

sections.label: Smaller cost-of-living support amount
sections.summary: The overall amount for cost-of-living support in this Budget is smaller than in previous years' Budgets because inflation has eased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In fact, if you look at the overall amount provided for cost-of-living support in this Budget, it is smaller than in previous years' Budgets – overall amount, not just vouchers alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If you look at the overall amount, it is smaller.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And one reason why it is smaller, is precisely because inflation has eased and we think it is correct to taper the overall size of the Cost-of-Living Support Package.

sections.label: CPF redesign and Special Account rate
sections.summary: The question is whether the CPF system could be redesigned or updated, as beating the risk-free Special Account rate is not easy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But the question that I said just now goes back to not just having choices and options, but whether, on a more structured basis, is there some possibility of looking at redesigning or updating the CPF system?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And even with the kind of glide path, Target Date Fund that we talked about, it is not easy to achieve a better outcome across the board on a consistent basis than the risk-free Special Account rate of 4% and up to 6% with extra interest.

sections.label: Singapore fiscal position
sections.summary: A strong fiscal position for Singapore is not at the expense of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: A strong fiscal position for Singapore is not at the expense of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Top-ups to endowment and trust funds
sections.summary: In these two years, close to about $42 billion can be set aside for top-ups to endowment and trust funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Speaker, just one clarification, but a bit of a long one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I mentioned the point about the top-ups to endowment and trust funds, about how just in these two years, we can set aside close to about $42 billion.

sections.label: Budget surplus and reserves
sections.summary: MP asks about the $14 billion Budget surplus and whether reserves need replenishing after $40 billion COVID-19 spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My first question is, the Leader of Opposition has pointed out that this term of Government will have a Budget surplus of $14 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My second question is, does the Government believe that there is still a need to put back into the reserves for the $40 billion we spent on COVID-19?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Because we all know from the statistics, from the data provided by MAS, that we have already accumulated more than $300 billion more in official foreign reserves over the last few years.

sections.label: NIRC transfers to funds
sections.summary: MP asks the Prime Minister to confirm NIRC transfers to endowment and trust funds and the funds' total assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: One, can the Prime Minister confirm that, indeed, on average, Budget resources equivalent to about 80% of the NIRC every year are being transferred to endowment and trust funds, which will not all be spent in the allocated year, but reported as an expenditure in that year?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Two, what are the total assets under the funds as of today?

sections.label: Re-examining NIRC diversion
sections.summary: MP asks the Government to re-examine diverting NIRC resources to funds instead of social spending or GST and property tax hikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Can the Government re-examine the need to divert so much resources from the NIRC to endowment and trust funds, so that we can redirect these Budget resources to fund social spending increases or to relook at the need for the hike in GST and property tax increases?

sections.label: BTO price below $1 million
sections.summary: MP asks how the Government will keep BTO prices below $1 million as land costs rise with property prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Three, how is the Government going to ensure that the BTO price will stay below $1 million, as the land cost continues to increase in line with property price increases?

sections.label: No return to reserves
sections.summary: The speaker states the Government will not put money back into the reserves because structural surpluses are not expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: He talked about whether we will put back into reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I thought I made that clear in my speech: we will not be putting back into the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will not be able to because we do not expect structural surpluses.

sections.label: BTO affordability and VERS
sections.summary: The speaker says VERS is the solution and BTO flats will be priced so Singaporeans can always afford them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The solution is the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On BTO flats, how do we ensure affordability?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do so by making sure that the pricing of BTO flats will be done in such a way that Singaporeans will always be able to afford them.

sections.label: CPI data and GST inflation
sections.summary: The Department of Statistics collects CPI data properly and there is no basis to say the GST increase turbocharged inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Unless Mr Leong is accusing the Department of Statistics of not collecting CPI data properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have a proper system of collecting CPI, updating the basket, the inflation basket and the data is what it is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There is no basis to say that GST increase has "turbocharged" inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And even MAS itself, in its assessment, would have reflected that in its monetary policy statements.

sections.label: Corporate income tax and Budget 2025
sections.summary: Corporate income tax rose to 4%-plus of GDP, and without it and the GST increase, FY2025 would be in deficit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I said in my Budget Statement, if we were to plan on previous assumptions for corporate income tax, it would be about 3%-plus of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It has gone up to 4%-plus of GDP now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And when we plan for Budget 2025, we have assumed the higher base.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But without that unexpected increase on corporate income tax, without the GST rate increase, certainly FY2025, based on whatever we are proposing to spend in the Budget, would end up in a deficit.

sections.label: Investing in R&D and capabilities
sections.summary: Singapore invests in R&D, capabilities and workers so multinational enterprises see an ecosystem that adds value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have to improve our capabilities, offer a value proposition to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that is why we are investing in R&D, we are investing in capabilities, we are investing in Singaporean workers, so that the MNEs come here and they see in Singapore an ecosystem which they can plug into and which adds value to their operations.

sections.label: BTO flat pricing and subsidies
sections.summary: BTO flats are priced differently from the resale market with growing subsidies to keep housing affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Housing is one of them with, which we have discussed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And I have described exactly how we are helping to manage cost of living pressures precisely by pricing the BTO flats different from what is in the resale market, with growing subsidies, precisely to keep it affordable for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Assets under endowment and trust funds
sections.summary: A question is asked whether the Prime Minister can state the total assets kept under endowment and trust funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Government can reduce some expenditures but also reduce the taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, my first question is, can the Prime Minister answer my question as to what is the total amount of assets they are now being kept under the endowment and trust funds?

sections.label: BTO prices and Prime Plus schemes
sections.summary: A question is asked whether BTO prices would have exceeded $1 million without the Prime and Plus schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The next question, is it possible that without introducing the Prime and the Plus schemes, the BTO price would have already gone above $1 million?

sections.label: Population growth and HDB prices
sections.summary: A question asks whether Singaporeans may need faster population growth to 10 million to arrest HDB price decline, with collections returned to benefit Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Okay, my last question is, will we reach a point when Singaporeans are faced with no choice but to increase our population faster to 10 million, in order to arrest the decline in our HDB price?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Whatever we collect, we put it back to benefit Singapore and Singaporeans directly.

sections.label: VERS details to come
sections.summary: VERS is described as outstanding and details will be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On VERS, yes, we know that it is something outstanding and we will provide details.

sections.label: Plus and Prime subsidy framework
sections.summary: A Plus and Prime framework provides more subsidies to lower headline prices, with additional subsidies returned to HDB upon sale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And when I win the BTO, I will strike lottery".

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the right thing to do is to have a Plus and Prime framework where we provide more subsidies in order to bring down the headline price, make it affordable but, at the same time, when the person sells that flat, the additional subsidies is returned to HDB.

sections.label: HDB as nation building pillar
sections.summary: HDB remains an important pillar for nation building, aiming for a nation of home owners with continued policy finetuning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think it continues to be a very important key pillar for nation building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We want to ensure a nation of home owners and we will continue to finetune and improve HDB policies to make sure that every Singaporean who wants to, can own their own homes.
